title: Practical identifiability and parameter estimation of compartmental epidemiological models
abstractText: Abstract Practical parameter identifiability in ODE-based epidemiological models is a known issue, yet one that merits further study. It is essentially ubiquitous owing to noise and errors in real data. In this study, to avoid uncertainty stemming from data of unknown quality, simulated data with added noise are used to investigate practical identifiability in two distinct epidemiological models. Particular emphasis is placed on the role of initial conditions, which are assumed unknown, except those that are directly measured. Instead of just focusing on one method of estimation, we use and compare results from various broadly used methods, including maximum likelihood and Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) estimation. Among other findings, our analysis revealed that the MCMC estimator is overall more robust than the point estimators considered. Its estimates and predictions are improved when the initial conditions of certain compartments are fixed so that the model becomes globally identifiable. For the point estimators and as concerns the question of whether fixing or fitting the initial conditions that are not directly measured improves parameter estimates, we find that the answer is model-dependent. Specifically, in the standard susceptible-exposed-infected-recovered (SEIR) model, fixing the initial condition for the susceptible population S(0) improved parameter estimates, while this was not true when fixing the initial condition of the asymptomatic population in a more involved model. Our study corroborates the change in quality of parameter estimates upon usage of pre-peak or post-peak time series. Finally, our examples suggest that in the presence of significantly noisy data, the value of structural identifiability is moot.

title: Contagion and escalation of rule violations
abstractText: Abstract Human societies rely on rules to coordinate behaviour, sustain cooperation and maintain social order. Yet compliance can be fragile when rules are weakly enforced and individuals observe others violating them. Prior research shows that rule violations and other antisocial behaviours can spread through social influence, but less is known about how the severity of violations shapes these dynamics. In many real-world settings, rule-breaking occurs in degrees, from minor infractions to major violations, and individuals may not only imitate others but sometimes exceed the violations they observe. Here, we combine simulations and a behavioural experiment (n = 750) to study how the magnitude of observed rule violations shapes subsequent violations, and how this can generate escalation dynamics. Our simulations show that when individuals occasionally escalate beyond observed violations, even rare escalation can trigger a rapid shift from widespread compliance to collective rule-breaking. In our pre-registered experiment, observing major violations strongly increased rule-breaking, especially when committed by socially close others. Observing minor violations prompted many participants to follow suit and a minority to escalate beyond the violations they observed. Parameterizing the simulations with these behavioural responses shows that such escalators can disproportionately undermine collective compliance. These results highlight how asymmetric responses to rule violations and rare escalatory behaviour can transform small deviations into large-scale breakdowns of rule compliance.

title: Mean-field optimal control with stochastic leaders
abstractText: Abstract We consider interacting agent systems with a large number of stochastic agents influenced by a fixed number of external stochastic lead agents. Such settings arise, for example, in models of opinion dynamics, where a small number of leaders can steer the behaviour of a large population of followers. In this context, we study a partial mean-field limit where the number of followers tends to infinity, while the number of leaders stays constant. The partial mean-field limit dynamics is then given by a McKean–Vlasov stochastic differential equation (SDE) for the followers, coupled to a controlled Itô-SDE governing the dynamics of the lead agents. For a given cost functional that the lead agents seek to minimize, we show that the unique optimal control of the finite agent system converges to the optimal control of the limiting system. This establishes that the low-dimensional control of the partial (mean-field) system provides an effective approximation for controlling the high-dimensional finite agent system. In addition, we propose a stochastic gradient descent algorithm that can efficiently approximate the mean-field control. Our theoretical results are illustrated on an opinion dynamics model with lead agents, where the control objective is to drive the followers to reach consensus.

title: Fast and slow surfactants in turbulence-driven bubble breakup
abstractText: When a large air cavity breaks in a turbulent flow, it goes through very large deformations and cascading events of new interface formation, including elongated filaments and bubbles over a wide range of scales, with their rate of formation controlled by turbulence and capillary processes. We experimentally investigate the effects of surfactants and salt on the fragmentation of a large air cavity, and observe a fivefold increase of the number of bubbles being produced in some cases. We characterise the bubble size distribution resulting from successive breakups in such a transient configuration. For bubbles larger than the Hinze scale d Subscript upper H d H $d_H$ (defined as the balance between surface tension and turbulence stresses), we observe that bubble size distributions remain unchanged for all solutions tested. For bubbles below d Subscript upper H d H $d_H$ , however, we observe an increase of the number of bubbles produced and an associated steepening of the bubble size distribution upon the addition of surfactant or salt. This later effect is only visible for surfactants with an adsorption time scale that is fast enough compared with the rate at which new interfaces are being generated by turbulence.

title: Soil aggregate fragmentation reduces microbial diversity but enhances oxidative metabolism that drives carbon loss
abstractText: The escalating pace of anthropogenic activities is exacerbating soil organic carbon (SOC) loss and altering microbial community structure and ecological functions. However, how soil microbiomes reorganize under SOC dynamics and feed back to carbon depletion, especially at micro-to-millimeter scale remain unresolved. Here, croplands spanning a SOC gradient under varying cultivation duration were used to examine microbial diversity trajectories across bacteria, fungi and protists, together with carbon decomposition in bulk soils and individual aggregate fractions. Metagenomics, 13C‐tracing and literature synthesis were integrated to interlink microbial functions with alterations of carbon substrates and microenvironment. The results derived from these data imply that incorporating microscale physical structure and associated biological processes into SOC turnover models is paramount to develop practices improving biodiversity conservation and carbon persistence under intensifying anthropogenic activity and climate changes.

title: Dynamics-informed deep learning for predicting extreme events
abstractText: Abstract Predicting extreme events in high-dimensional chaotic dynamical systems remains a fundamental challenge because these events are rare, intermittent and often driven by transient dynamical mechanisms that are difficult to identify from limited observations. We propose a fully data-driven framework for real-time forecasting of extreme events based on an interpretable, mechanism-aware precursor that tracks the transient instabilities preceding event onset. Specifically, we use the finite-time Lyapunov exponent (FTLE) as the precursor, computed directly from state snapshots through a reduced-order, equation-agnostic formulation. By restricting the instability dynamics to an adaptively evolving subspace spanned by optimal time-dependent (OTD) modes, the method substantially reduces the computational cost of classical FTLE evaluation while retaining the dominant transiently amplifying directions. The resulting FTLE sequence serves as input to a transformer-based model that forecasts the system observable at future lead times, enabling long-lead prediction of extreme events. We demonstrate the framework on Kolmogorov flow, a canonical model of intermittent turbulence. The results show that explicitly encoding transient instability mechanisms substantially extends extreme-event prediction horizons compared to baseline observable-based approaches.

title: Intra- and Interlayer Excitonic Fine Structure of the Two-Dimensional Perovskite (PEA)2PbI4
abstractText: Abstract Two-dimensional halide perovskites host strongly bound excitons whose fine structure governs polarization selection rules and radiative recombination, yet spectral features in phenethylammonium lead iodide ((PEA)2PbI4) remain controversially assigned. Here, polarization-resolved low-temperature photoluminescence (PL) combined with first-principles G0W0+BSE calculations probes the intralayer and interlayer excitonic fine structure of this Ruddlesden–Popper perovskite. The low-energy multiplet is consistent with the intralayer excitonic fine structure governed by electron–hole exchange, crystal symmetry, and layer inequivalence in the two-layer unit cell, without requiring Rashba effects or exciton–polaron mechanisms as its primary origin. The weak doublet about 40 meV higher is best accounted for by interlayer excitons based on its energetics, splitting, and real-space character. Distortion-induced mixing of interlayer excitons with bright intralayer excitons provides a plausible explanation for the observed interlayer PL intensities and nearly orthogonal polarizations. These results support a layer-resolved excitonic picture encompassing both intralayer and interlayer states in (PEA)2PbI4.

title: Efficacy of statistical and design interventions for improving reproducibility in biomedical research
abstractText: Abstract Over the past two decades, failures to replicate published findings in biomedical research have led to a perceived reproducibility crisis. Several interventions at the level of inferential statistics and experimental design have been proposed for improving reproducibility. These include raising the power by increasing the sample size, redefining the threshold for statistical significance, focusing on a minimally important difference, adding a penalising term for between-study variation, and combining data from multiple study centres. We used simulations to investigate the effectiveness of these interventions on measures of reproducibility. Artificial data sets were created by repeatedly sampling from defined parametric distributions based on published biomedical studies (i.e. real-world data sets). Reproducibility measures included the probability of positive findings, the probability of consistent inferential outcomes and the chance of capturing the true effect size. The results were mixed: some of the proposed interventions could improve reproducibility, while others had detrimental effects on reproducibility. Notably, the interventions affected the various aspects of reproducibility differently.

title: Electronic Spectroscopy of Atomic Defects in Molybdenum Disulfide under Ambient Conditions
abstractText: Abstract We present results of electronic spectroscopy experiments performed on individual defects in the prototypical transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD) molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) under ambient conditions by way of conductive atomic force microscopy (C-AFM). Data acquired in the form of consecutive, high-resolution current maps at various bias voltages allow the assessment of local conductivity and differential conductance as a function of bias voltage for individual defects, the effects of which range from single-atomic sites to several nanometers in lateral size. Characteristic behavior in spectroscopy data allows the categorization of observed defects into distinct groups and provides clues with regard to their chemical identities.

title: Bistability of midpoint-fused arches with pinned-pinned boundary conditions
abstractText: Abstract Arranging multiple arches in a circular pattern and fusing them at their midpoint yields a three-dimensional configuration that we refer to as midpoint-fused arches (MFA). This study investigates the structural bistability of MFA, i.e. their ability to admit two distinct, force-free stable equilibrium states. Starting from an as-fabricated, stress-free configuration, MFA can invert into a stressed, toggled state reminiscent of an umbrella’s ribs. We develop an analytical model for the response of a pinned-pinned MFA subjected to a concentrated midspan load by minimizing the total potential energy. Individual arches are treated as spatially deforming, and kinematic-compatibility relations are derived at the fusion point to couple their deformations. Various deformation symmetries are then exploited to simplify the problem. We demonstrate the model’s utility by characterizing the force-displacement response of a two-arch MFA, identifying distinct deformation pathways and discussing the pathway transitions that occur during toggling. In particular, we show how the structure switches between symmetric and asymmetric deformation modes as it moves between stable configurations. The generality of the framework is further established through analysis of a three-arch MFA, which exhibits richer coupled deformation behaviour. Nonlinear finite-element simulations and tabletop experiments corroborate the analytical predictions, showing close agreement in both equilibrium states and the associated transition responses.

title: Caribbean Islands facilitated the colonization of Western Hemisphere barn owls, yet experienced rampant extinction
abstractText: Abstract Island biodiversity reflects multiple evolutionary roles, encompassing lineages derived from nearby continents, relict taxa and, in limited cases, sources of continental diversity. Reconstructing the biogeographic history and island-mainland diversification dynamics requires an integrated understanding of speciation, extinction and dispersal processes to and from islands. Extensive Holocene extinctions may obscure patterns of diversity and connectivity. Tytonidae (barn and bay owls) is a bird group with a worldwide distribution and numerous Quaternary extinctions. Here, we use ultraconserved elements and mitogenomes extracted from tissues, historical museum specimens and fossils to reconstruct phylogenetic relationships and colonization pathways, with a focus on Western Hemisphere taxa. We also summarize extinct Tyto diversity to evaluate Quaternary diversity trends. Our results align with previous studies in supporting an Eastern origin for Western Hemisphere Tyto. We found that the Caribbean was, and still is, the centre of Tyto diversity in the Western Hemisphere, although nearly all Caribbean Tyto (and their mammalian prey) are now extinct. Unexpectedly, we identified two independent Tyto colonization events of the Galápagos. Our study provides strong evidence that islands can serve as sources of diversity for some continental lineages, as well as museums of diversity that harbour unique lineages prone to disturbance-driven extinction.

title: The Women's Baths: Female Agency, Medical Knowledge, and The Healing Body in Late Renaissance Italy
abstractText: Abstract This article examines the overlooked role of women in shaping medical and cultural practices at Renaissance spas, with a focus on Bagni di Lucca in Tuscany. Drawing on a heterogeneous body of sources, including letters, medical treatises, architectural evidence, and material culture, it reconstructs women's experiences as patients, patrons, and participants in balneological culture. While early modern physicians prescribed thermal baths for a wide range of ailments, particularly female infertility, women's correspondence reveals more situated and active engagements with hydrotherapy. Letters by noblewomen such as Isabella di Capua illustrate observation and familiarity with humoral theory, while those by Ginevra Gozzadini show how therapeutic routines could intersect with spiritual reflection. Attending closely to the material settings of the baths and to the bodily routines they imposed, the article explores the sensory, affective, and mnemonic dimensions of bathing. It highlights how taste, heat, touch, temporality, and ritualized practice shaped perceptions of illness and cure within broader structures of medical authority and social hierarchy. By foregrounding women's voices and embodied experience, the article complicates physician‑centred accounts of early modern hydrotherapy and reappraises the spa as a site of negotiation between medical prescription and lived practice, elite and vernacular knowledge, and body and belief.

abstractText: Penetapan Upah Minimum Kabupaten/Kota (UMK) merupakan instrument penting dalam kebijakan ketenagakerjaan Indonesia yang bertujuan melindungi hak-hak pekerja sekaligus menjaga keseimbangan hubungan industrial. Penelitian ini mengkaji kewenangan Disnakertrans Jatim dalam mendampingi Gubernur pada sengketa penetapan UMK 2025 berdasarkan AUPB. Studi kasus yang digunakan adalah gugatan Serikat Pekerja FSP Kahutindo di PTUN SBY (Putusan No. 11/G/2025/PTUN.SBY). Metode yang digunakan ialah penelitian hukum empiris bersifat deskriptif analitis dengan pendekatan induktif-deduktif, melalui wawancara mendalam dan analisis dokumen. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan Gubernur Jawa Timur menetapkan kenaikan UMK sebesar 5% tanpa justifikasi tertulis yang memadai, menyimpang dari formula imperatif 6,5% sesuai PP Nomor 51 Tahun 2023. PTUN Surabaya menyatakan keputusan tersebut melanggar asas kepastian hukum dan asas kecermatan. Disnakertrans menghadapi kendala regulasi, kelembagaan, dan kapasitas penanganan sengketa. Sebagai respons, Disnakertrans berkomitmen melakukan perbaikan komprehensif meliputi penyempurnaan SOP, penguatan koordinasi multi-stakeholder, dan peningkatan kapasitas hukum pegawai.

title: Efektivitas Komunikasi Celebrity Endorsment Raffi Ahmad Dalam Mempertahankan Kepercayaan Konsumen Roti Aoka Atas Kasus Dugaan Kandungan Bahan Berbahaya di Aceh
abstractText: Isu dugaan kandungan bahan berbahaya pada Roti Aoka menimbulkan krisis kepercayaan konsumen, yang ditanggapi perusahaan dengan melibatkan Raffi Ahmad sebagai celebrity endorser. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis efektivitas komunikasi celebrity endorsement tersebut dalam membangun kepercayaan konsumen berdasarkan Source Credibility Theory serta mengidentifikasi perbedaan distribusi opini publik di TikTok sebelum dan sesudah endorsement. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan analisis isi terhadap 100 komentar TikTok yang dipilih secara purposive sampling, terdiri atas 23 komentar sebelum dan 77 sesudah endorsement. Pengodean dilakukan oleh dua coder dengan koefisien reliabilitas Holsti 1,00. Data dianalisis melalui distribusi frekuensi serta uji Chi-Square. Opini publik bergeser dari 100% netral sebelum endorsement menjadi 66,2% percaya dan 33,8% netral sesudahnya, tanpa komentar tidak percaya. Indikasi trustworthiness dan attractiveness muncul pada 66,2% komentar sesudah endorsement, sedangkan expertise tidak terindikasi. Uji independensi menunjukkan hubungan signifikan (χ² = 100,00), sedangkan proporsi opini positif sebesar 51% tidak berbeda signifikan dari 50% (χ² = 0,04). Hubungan sempurna tersebut perlu dibaca hati-hati karena kemungkinan tumpang tindih pengodean. Endorsement berkaitan dengan terbentuknya kepercayaan awal yang bertumpu pada keterpercayaan dan daya tarik, sehingga perlu dilengkapi bukti teknis dari lembaga berwenang

The Depth of Problem Definition: Evaluating Pre-Service Mathematics Teachers’ Initial PCK through Post-Case Study Diagnosis
abstractText: This qualitative embedded single-case study examined how pre-service mathematics teachers in Eastern Indonesia define pedagogical problems after school-based case studies and how the depth of those definitions differs across initial pedagogical content knowledge (PCK) categories. Six purposively selected sixth-semester students, two each in low, moderate, and high initial-PCK groups, were selected from 44 questionnaire respondents. Data comprised post-case-study reports, an initial-PCK questionnaire, and semi-structured interviews. The data were analyzed through a reflexive thematic procedure involving data condensation, coding, theme development, and cross-category comparison, with triangulation, peer debriefing, member checking, and an audit trail. All participants identified conceptual and procedural difficulties, prerequisite gaps, and modeling obstacles. However, low-PCK participants predominantly described surface symptoms; moderate-PCK participants mapped error patterns and prerequisite weaknesses using evidence; and high-PCK participants constructed precise, evidence-based, multidimensional diagnoses spanning cognitive, affective, and metacognitive dimensions. Topic complexity was treated as an analytic condition rather than a basis for causal inference by comparing the structure and evidential quality of definitions within each case and then across PCK categories. The findings position problem definition as an observable expression of pedagogical reasoning and support explicit, scaffolded diagnostic-competence learning in mathematics teacher education, especially in resource-constrained and diverse educational settings. Keywords: pre-service mathematics teachers, problem definition, initial pedagogical content knowledge, eastern indonesia.

Analysis of the Copyrightability of Artificial Intelligence-Generated Content in the United States
abstractText: The commercial application of generative artificial intelligence has rapidly brought to the fore the structural tension between machine-generated content (AIGC) and the core presuppositions of copyright law concerning the “author.” This paper examines the protection model and legal mechanisms adopted by the United States on the question of AIGC copyrightability. The research finds that the United States, as represented by the Thaler case, strengthens the “human authorship” requirement from the perspectives of constitutional text, statutory interpretation, and incentive theory, and adopts a result-oriented standard centered on expressive control.

title: Assessing primary health care network preparedness for future pandemics in Lebanon
abstractText: Abstract Background The COVID-19 pandemic exposed critical gaps in health system preparedness worldwide, particularly within primary health care (PHC). In Lebanon, disparities between rural and urban and INGO-supported and non-INGO-supported primary health care centers (PHCCs) may affect the ability of PHCCs to respond to future pandemics. The Health Emergency Preparedness, Response and Resilience (HEPR) framework provides a structured approach to assess facility-level preparedness. Aim To assess PHC preparedness for future pandemics in Lebanon and identify gaps requiring improvement. Methods A health facility survey was administered to 185 eligible PHCCs nationwide, with 169 responses (91.4%). Findings were mapped across the 5 HEPR domains and analyzed using descriptive and unadjusted bivariate statistics, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05. Results Preparedness varied across HEPR domains. Timely reporting of priority communicable diseases through the national surveillance system was reported by 99.4% of PHCCs, whereas no PHCC reported a formal feedback mechanism to systematically address community concerns. Only 53.8% of PHCCs reported having an emergency plan, indicating an important gap in facility-level emergency preparedness. Countermeasures were readily available, although availability varied across vaccines, medicines, laboratory networks, and essential supplies. Conclusion PHC pandemic preparedness in Lebanon showed strengths in surveillance and access to countermeasures but persistent gaps in emergency coordination, workforce preparedness, risk communication, and sustainable financing. This study demonstrates how a national HEPR framework can be operationalized at the PHC facility level, offering a practical approach for strengthening preparedness in fragile and crisis-affected settings.

title: Regulatory Evolution of δ-MnO2 Active Sites Enhances Ozone Decomposition
abstractText: Abstract Ozone (O3) pollution arising from rapid urbanization poses a significant threat to both the air quality and human health. Manganese dioxide, a widely studied material, typically exhibits limited performance due to the occupation of oxygen vacancy (Vo) sites by water and reaction intermediates. In this work, we tailored the surface coordination environment via heat treatment, yielding a series of catalysts with varying numbers of hydroxyl groups and Vo sites. Characterization results revealed that surface hydroxyl groups not only serve as supplementary reactive sites but also modulate the electronic properties of Vo sites, thereby effectively lowering the desorption energy of the intermediate species. Notably, superior catalytic activity was achieved even at a relatively low density of Vo sites. In situ DRIFTs were employed to systematically monitor the reaction intermediates and track the reaction evolution. Complementary DFT calculations further elucidated the accompanying changes in the electronic structure and reaction pathways. This work deepens the mechanistic understanding of catalytic O3 decomposition, offers valuable guidance for rational structural design, and facilitates its practical applications.

title: Sex differences in the diabetes-related risk of incident myocardial infarction and relationship to established CHD risk factors. The Tromsø Study (1979-2016)
abstractText: Abstract Aim To examine whether the adverse effect of diabetes on the risk of incident myocardial infarction (MI) differs between sexes and assess to what extent established coronary heart disease (CHD) risk factors contribute to the elevated risk. Methods Prospective study of 42,907 Tromsø Study participants (51.5% women) with 3942 incident MI (357 with diabetes) at ages 35–104 years. Relative risks (IRR) were estimated in Poisson regression analyses. Impact of CHD risk factors was quantified as percentage change in the regression coefficient for diabetes. Results A contrast in risk of MI by diabetes status was seen from age 45 in men and 55 in women. Adjusted for age and birth-cohort, the IRR was 2.26 in women and 1.84 in men (p = 0.12, test for interaction). In a mutually adjusted model, adjustment for the triglyceride to HDL-cholesterol ratio weakened the association with diabetes similarly in women (-19.0%) and men (−17.0%), systolic blood pressure had larger impact in women (-10.3% vs. + 2.2%), whereas smoking strengthened the association more in men (+23.1% vs. + 7.1%). Body mass index had minor impact. A larger joint impact of adjustment factors in women (-33.6% vs. -15.9%) narrowed the initial gender gap (adjusted IRR of 1.72 and 1.67 respectively). Adverse lipid levels and increasing systolic blood pressure emerged already during the pre-diabetic phase. Conclusions Traditional CHD risk factors contributed substantially to the diabetes-related risk of incident MI. A larger joint impact of these factors in women reduced the initial observed sex difference in the adverse effect of diabetes.

Implementasi Sistem Informasi Analisis Laboratorium Berbasis Web pada PT Multi Nitrotama Kimia Karawang
abstractText: Quality control in the chemical industry requires accurate and timely recording of process parameters. At PT Multi Nitrotama Kimia, laboratory results from three production plants—the Ammonium Nitrate Plant, Nitric Acid Plant, and Utility Plant—were recorded on paper logsheets and compiled in separate spreadsheets. This practice increased transcription errors, delayed report circulation, and provided no automatic warnings for parameters exceeding specified limits. This study aims to develop ANLAB, a web-based Laboratory Analysis Information System. The system was developed using the Waterfall model, PHP, CodeIgniter 3, and MySQL. Data were collected through observations, interviews with analysts, Distributed Control System (DCS) operators and supervisors, and document reviews. ANLAB features digital forms that classify results as normal, above, or below limits; a three-tier approval workflow; additional check requests; plant shutdown tagging; role-based access control; and PDF and Excel report exports. Black box testing involving 27 scenarios confirmed that all tested functions produced the expected results. However, testing focused exclusively on functionality; time savings, error reduction, and paperless performance were not measured. Future evaluations should assess these indicators using system timestamps. The findings indicate that ANLAB provides a structured and traceable digital workflow for laboratory data management in chemical plant operations

title: Extended in-use stability of Krebs von den Lungen-6 (KL-6) reagents, quality controls, and calibrators under refrigerated conditions
abstractText: Reliable diagnostic testing depends on the stability of assay compo-nents, including reagents, quality controls (QCs), and calibrators. For the Nanopia KL-6 assay used in interstitial lung disease (ILD) assessment, the manufacturer states that in-use stability is limited to 1 month for reagents and QCs and approximately 2.5 months for calibrators at 2–8°C. This study evaluated the extended in-use stability of Nanopia KL-6 reagents, QCs, and calibrators for up to four months under refrigerated conditions. Extended stability testing was performed at seven prede-fined time points (T0–T6) over 132 days. Reagent stability was assessed using in-use QC materials at two concentration levels. QC stability was evaluated by aliquoting and testing stored QC material over time. Cali-brators stability was assessed across four concentration levels using bias analyses. Reagents and QCs demonstrated acceptable analytical stability for up to 132 days, with increasing bias observed beyond Day 90. All calibrator levels remained stable for up to 132 days with minimal bias (<10%). Nanopia KL-6 reagents, QCs and all calibrator levels remain sta-ble for up to 132 days when stored at 2–8°C, provided appropriate qual-ity monitoring is implemented.

Microgrid Protection Enhancement Using Voltage Restrained Overcurrent Relay: Case Study of Semau Island
abstractText: The adoption of renewable energy sources in microgrids has increased rapidly in recent years; some microgrids operate in a hybrid operation, full supply from PV during the day and using diesel at night. The increase in inverter-based renewable energy sources has an impact on the character of the network when a short circuit occurs. In synchronous generator-based power plants, the short-circuit contribution current generated is very large. Meanwhile, in inverter-based power plants, the short-circuit current generated is not much different from the nominal current. Under these conditions, conventional overcurrent protection relays are no longer effective in protecting the network, so development is needed so that the network remains safe and disturbances can be isolated properly and quickly. The proposed relay is a voltage-limited overcurrent relay. It should detect disturbances and quickly isolate them in both synchronous generator-based and inverter-based sources. Simulation of the resulting settings is carried out using ETAP software. The results of this study indicate that when generating only from PV, the overcurrent relay does not operate when there is a short circuit. After VR-OCR is activated, the relay can operate with a time of 857 ms.

Adverse events in paediatric spinal deformity surgery – 12-year review of specialist spinal deformity practice
abstractText: Aims Adverse events following paediatric spinal deformity surgery in the UK suffers from significant reporting gaps, as current data relies predominantly on voluntary incident submissions. This retrospective study aims to comprehensively assess the incidence of all surgical adverse events at a specialized paediatric spinal orthopaedic centre. Methods A retrospective review of prospectively collected data from January 2010 to December 2022 systematically evaluated perioperative and postoperative adverse events. Patients were analyzed by scoliosis aetiology and adverse events were stratified according to the Clavien-Dindo classification system. Adverse events were further grouped by common themes including implant-related, infection-related, and neurological events. Results A total of 871 paediatric spinal deformity patients undergoing 1,020 operations with at least two years follow-up were identified. Adolescent idiopathic scoliosis was the most common primary pathology with 545 patients (62.6%). Overall, 324 patients (37.2%) experienced an adverse event. Adverse events were categorized by severity: 14.8% grade 1, 5.3% grade 2, 1.1% grade 3A, 14.6% grade 3B, 1.1% grade 4, and 0.1% grade 5. Implant-related issues were most frequent (n = 113, 13.0%), followed by curve progression (n = 33, 3.8%) and persistent pain (n = 33, 3.8%). Neurological events included four complete cord injuries (0.5%) and four incomplete cord injuries which fully recovered (0.5%). One perioperative death occurred. Conclusion In this cohort of paediatric spinal deformity surgeries, over one-third of patients experienced adverse events, predominantly of low severity requiring minimal or no further intervention. Implant-related adverse events were most frequent, while the incidence of both complete and incomplete spinal cord injury, as well as mortality, remained reassuringly low across all procedures. title: Rate Coefficients for the OH Reaction with CF3SCF3: Atmospheric Lifetime and Global Warming Potential
abstractText: Abstract Bis(trifluoromethyl) sulfide (CF3SCF3) is a candidate insulating gas whose atmospheric persistence is poorly constrained: the structure–activity relationship cannot be reliably extrapolated to this perfluorinated species, and the only available theoretical estimate has not yet been tested against experiment. We measured the rate coefficient of its dominant atmospheric loss, reaction with OH, by pulsed laser photolysis–laser-induced fluorescence over 272–328 K at 50 Torr. The reaction is slow and nearly temperature independent, with k1(298 K) = (2.15 ± 0.34) × 10–15 cm3 molecule–1 s–1 and a slight positive trend (apparent Ea = (0.30 ± 0.14) kcal mol–1). No O2 dependence was detectable at 50 Torr. The measured k1 exceeds the theoretical value by approximately an order of magnitude, implying an OH-initiated lifetime of ∼14.7 years and a 100-year GWP of ∼2570, well below that of SF6 (24300), supporting further evaluation of CF3SCF3 as an alternative dielectric gas.

title: Palaeoproteomic investigation of archaeological sediments associated with ochre use in the Middle Stone Age of southern Africa
abstractText: Abstract The African Middle Stone Age (MSA) represents the cultural and technological context associated with the emergence of Homo sapiens and the development of complex cognition. In this setting, ochre use is considered a multifaceted proxy for modern behaviour, allowing inferences about technical and symbolic aspects of Homo sapiens. Powdered ochre is reported in multiple southern African ethnographic and archaeological contexts alongside various organic materials, some of which are protein-based. Yet, the recovery of proteinaceous residues is rare in the MSA. Since proteins can offer insights into their tissue and species of origin, identifying proteins in association with ochre may help to infer its function. At Klipdrift Shelter (South Africa), the 60 000-year-old Howiesons Poort layers contain a laterally continuous, ochre-rich sediment surface, possibly over 1 m long, 40 cm wide, and up to 1 cm thick. We used palaeoproteomics to identify proteinaceous traces from this feature. Our analysis identified type I collagen confidently matching common eland (Taurotragus oryx) in two samples. Together with the feature's highly complex nature, these findings suggest the deliberate mixing of eland-derived proteins with ochre powder. Our results confirm that palaeoproteomics can be a reliable tool for reconstructing the protein component of the early human material culture.

title: Baseline and early changes in serum proteomic profiles predict anti-tumor activity in patients with advanced HPV-associated malignancies treated with novel combination immunotherapy
abstractText: Abstract Background Patients with advanced human papillomavirus (HPV)–associated malignancies who do not respond to immune checkpoint blockade have limited treatment options. Combination immunotherapy consisting of an HPV16 therapeutic peptide cancer vaccine (PDS0101) to initiate an immune response, a tumor-targeting IL-12 immunocytokine (PDS01ADC) to potentiate that response, and a bifunctional agent providing dual blockade of programmed cell death ligand 1 (PD-L1) and transforming growth factor β (TGF-β) (bintrafusp alfa) to reduce immunosuppression has demonstrated promising clinical activity in a prior report of a clinical trial in patients with advanced HPV16 + –associated malignancies (NCT04287868). Here, we provide updated clinical results from that trial and identify immune correlates of clinical response. Methods We performed a comprehensive survey of the peripheral immunome from 38 patients with HPV16 + tumors, and built machine-learning models using a survey of serum proteomic data to predict which patients would derive clinical benefit and improved overall survival from treatment. Results Models incorporating baseline levels of IL- 6 and heme oxygenase 1, alone or with an early change in granzyme B, effectively predicted clinical benefit and duration of overall survival. We also identified a persistent skewing of increased peripheral CD8 + T cells to myeloid cell ratios in patients who benefit from treatment. Moreover, there was a positive association between monocyte and myeloid derived suppressor cell frequencies with serum concentrations of inhibitory biomarkers, providing biological rationale of the serum-based prediction models. Conclusions Although retrospective, these data demonstrate outcome prediction in patients with HPV-associated malignancies using readily quantifiable molecular correlates from minimally invasive sampling of peripheral blood prior to therapy or early in the regimen and thus provide the rationale for prospective validation in future clinical studies.

title: Component-based approach to assessing the applicability of large language models in decision support systems
abstractText: The article proposes a component-based approach to assessing the applicability of large language models in decision support systems. The necessity of multidimensional evaluation is substantiated, and an original methodology for component-based assessment is presented, taking into account both the content of the text and its suitability for specific applied contexts. Unlike existing review scales, the approach suggests the use of operational applicability profiles of the response and a decision-making procedure at the level of a specific output. The components capture verifiable properties of the response and serve as the basis for reproducible metrics and evaluation criteria. The approach is oriented toward typical decision support system tasks and can be applied in both expert and automated scenarios. The methodology can be used to verify generated results and enhance the substantiation of trust in them.

title: Optimal quasi-adiabatic path in a two-level system
abstractText: Abstract We consider a generic two-level quantum system with control parameters as the coupling between the two states, taking values in a bounded positive interval, and the detuning, restricted in a symmetric interval around zero. Using Stokes theorem, we prove that the optimal path for fast quasi-adiabatic dynamics lies mainly on the border of parameter space, as it was numerically found in a recent study regarding coupled elastic waveguides, modelled as a two-level system. We calculate analytically the adiabaticity parameter as a function of the protocol duration and compare with the finite-time Landau–Zener protocol, where the coupling is kept constant while the detuning varies linearly with time. The optimized-path protocol shows superior performance even for shorter durations, where the Landau–Zener protocol fails. The present study may be useful in different fields with systems modelled as the investigated generic two-level quantum system.

title: Room-Temperature Visible-Light Single-Photon Avalanche Detection in Grating-Coupled Post-CMOS Photonic Circuits
abstractText: Abstract The integration of photonic circuits with on-chip single-photon detectors has emerged as a key enabling technology for highly scalable visible-wavelength photonic integrated circuits, underpinning advanced applications in quantum information processing and biophotonics. However, detecting weak optical signals down to the single-photon regime at specific wavelengths requires efficient interconnections between photonic waveguides and detectors. Here, we present an interconnect from silicon nitride photonic circuits to single-photon avalanche diodes (SPADs) on a standard 200 mm CMOS wafer integrated using post-CMOS integration. To realize this efficient interconnect, we optimized the interface by introducing metal reflector-assisted grating couplers for the target wavelengths 633 nm and 785 nm. To investigate the influence of the reflector on the efficiency of the interface, we conducted simulations and subsequent optimizations. In simulation, the grating-assisted interconnect achieves a coupling efficiency of 2.0 dB at 785 nm, representing a 6.4 dB improvement over the baseline design. To validate this improvement, we fabricated this structure with and without reflector and experimentally demonstrate detection of single photons at the target wavelengths. After post-CMOS integration, the utilized Fraunhofer IMS SPADs were operated at room temperature with an off-chip passive quenching circuit. Optical characterization showed an improvement by up to 4.5 dB by implementing reflectors. We show venues for improving the photon detection probability by correlating it with loss sources encountered in the fabricated devices. With these results, we demonstrate the applicability of post-CMOS integration and offer a photonic-integrated solution for detecting single photons from red to near-infrared wavelengths.

title: Tunable Lewis Acidity of B(mdan): A Balance between Stability and Reactivity
abstractText: Abstract The Lewis acidities of organoboron compounds are pivotal in determining the reactivity and selectivity of boron-based synthetic transformations. Moreover, the stability of organoboron compounds is closely linked to their Lewis acidities, which are significantly influenced by substituents such as pinacolato (pin) and naphthalene-1,8-diaminato (dan). This study introduces the adaptive nature of an untapped N,N′-dimethyl-1,8-diaminonaphthalene-substituted boron functionality, B(mdan), demonstrating its ability to modulate Lewis acidities between H–B(mdan) and Ar–B(mdan), which is unachievable with B(pin) and B(dan). Lewis acidity-diminished and thus robust H–B(mdan) is directly convertible into an array of Ar–B(mdan) upon treatment with Grignard and organolithium reagents. The resulting Ar–B(mdan) exhibits 1.5 times greater Lewis acidity and serves as sufficiently reactive carbon nucleophiles, facilitating efficient, weak base-promoted, palladium-catalyzed direct cross-coupling reactions. Deviations in Lewis acidities, arising from different substituents (mdan, pin, and dan) and organic groups (H and Ph), as well as a detailed mechanism of the key transmetalation are systematically studied through computational techniques, including ammonia affinity, deformation/interaction enthalpy, and IGMH analysis.

title: Consistent diversity loss but divergent functional responses of freshwater biofilms to salinity and nutrient enrichment across climatic regions
abstractText: Abstract Freshwater salinization and nutrient enrichment are intensifying globally. Despite their widespread co-occurrence, the generality of their combined effects across regions remains unclear, limiting identification of appropriate policy scales. Using outdoor freshwater ponds established >10 years ago, replicated across inland, coastal and mountain regions, we examined independent and interactive effects of elevated salinity (0, +5 and +15 g NaCl l⁻¹) and nutrient enrichment (10 : 1 N : P additions) on benthic biofilms. Salinity was the dominant driver of community structure and function. Nutrient enrichment increased green algae abundances after 30 days but did not affect biofilm function or bacterial structure. Across all regions, bacterial richness and Shannon's diversity index declined consistently with increasing salinity after 30 days and bacterial community structures differed among all salinity levels by 60 days. Responses of phototrophic groups and biofilm functions, however, were region-specific. In the inland region, high salinity increased biofilm biomass, gross primary productivity (GPP), net primary productivity (NPP) and abundances of diatoms and cyanobacteria; in the coastal region, GPP and NPP declined under high salinity with no change to phototroph abundances; while neither was affected in the mountain region. In sum, taxonomic changes in biofilm bacterial communities under salinization were consistent across regions, while functional changes varied.

title: Digital Trust and Personalization Strategy As Drivers Of Customer Retention In E-Commerce: A Structural Equation Modeling Approach
abstractText: This study examines the relationships between digital trust, personalization strategy, and customer retention in e-commerce. A quantitative explanatory survey design and purposive sampling were used to collect responses from e-commerce users who had completed online purchases and experienced platform features such as product recommendations or promotional offers. The questionnaire measured digital trust, personalization strategy, and customer retention using a five-point Likert scale. Data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling–Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS), including assessment of indicator loadings, convergent validity, internal consistency reliability, path coefficients, bootstrapped significance, and explained variance (R²). The manuscript supplied for revision does not report the final sample size, respondent profile, indicator statistics, path coefficients, p-values, or R² values; these results must be inserted from the original dataset before the abstract can make a defensible statement about effect strength or statistical significance. Conceptually, the study considers digital trust and personalization as related dimensions of e-commerce customer relationship management. The study’s contribution is to examine both constructs in one model while recognizing that claims about their relationships with retention must be supported by the empirical estimates.

Associations of loneliness, multidimensional self-care, and widowhood with health-related quality of life among older adults in Greece
abstractText: Abstract Background Loneliness is consistently associated with poorer health-related quality of life in older adulthood. However, marital status alone may not adequately represent the subjective and everyday processes associated with health, and the role of multidimensional self-care in this context remains insufficiently understood. Objective This study examined the associations of loneliness and multidimensional self-care with mental and physical health-related quality of life among community-dwelling older adults and assessed whether self-care statistically accounted for part of these cross-sectional associations beyond widowed status and other relevant characteristics. Methods A cross-sectional observational study was conducted among community-dwelling older adults recruited across Greece between July 2024 and July 2025 through community centres, primary healthcare units, municipal social services, and local associations. Data on the principal study variables were available for 608 participants. Age data were available for 607 participants, who were aged 62–99 years (M = 77.61, SD = 8.53), and 63.5% of the sample were women. Fully adjusted regression and indirect-effect models included 607 complete cases. Participants completed the De Jong Gierveld Loneliness Scale, the Multidimensional Self-Care Scale for Older Adults, and the SF-36. Pearson correlations, independent-samples t tests, hierarchical multiple regressions, and cross-sectional indirect-effect analyses with 10,000 bootstrap resamples were performed. Post hoc sensitivity analyses were also conducted using outcome-specific self-care scores that excluded the domains most directly overlapping with the respective health outcomes. Results Greater loneliness was associated with poorer aggregated mental ( r = − .57) and physical health ( r = − .50), whereas higher multidimensional self-care was associated with better mental ( r = .69) and physical health ( r = .70; all p < .001). The final regression models explained 52.7% of the variance in mental health and 54.7% of the variance in physical health. In the fully adjusted models, self-care showed the strongest independent association with both mental (β = 0.494, p < .001) and physical health (β = 0.511, p < .001). Loneliness remained negatively associated with mental (β = −0.216, p < .001) and physical health (β = −0.085, p = .025), whereas widowed status was not independently associated with either outcome. Statistically supported indirect associations through self-care were observed for mental health (B = − 6.91, 95% bootstrap CI [− 8.33, − 5.59]) and physical health (B = − 9.14, 95% bootstrap CI [− 10.94, − 7.38]). In post hoc sensitivity analyses, the self-care associations were attenuated but remained statistically significant after the most directly overlapping domains were excluded (mental health: β = 0.311; physical health: β = 0.310; both p < .001), and the corresponding indirect associations remained statistically supported. Conclusions Loneliness and multidimensional self-care were independently associated with mental and physical health-related quality of life, whereas widowed status did not retain an independent association after adjustment. Self-care statistically accounted for part of the contemporaneous associations between loneliness and health. Sensitivity analyses indicated that conceptual overlap contributed to the magnitude of these associations but did not fully account for them. Because the data were cross-sectional, these findings do not establish temporal ordering or causal mediation. They nevertheless support the joint assessment of subjective loneliness and multidimensional self-care rather than reliance on marital status alone when examining health in later life.

The role of genetic distance in modulating intraspecific plant–soil interactions among a diverse assemblage of tropical tree species seedlings
abstractText: Abstract Microbial specialization on host species can promote plant diversity through plant–soil interactions that affect seedling survival and performance. While these processes are typically studied at the interspecific level, emerging evidence suggests that plant–soil interactions can be genotype-specific, contributing to intraspecific density dependence (iDD). However, iDD remains poorly understood in tropical tree species, particularly with respect to its strength and frequency. We hypothesized that genetic distance among conspecific trees should modulate the strength of iDD, and the direction of the effect—positive or negative seedling response—should reflect the net balance of plant–microbe antagonistic and mutualistic interactions. Using a reciprocal planting experiment across eight tropical tree species, we show that genetic distance between conspecific individuals significantly influences seedling responses, consistent with iDD. Yet, the direction of this effect was variable: Castilla tunu showed higher survival and Wettinia aequalis greater biomass in soils from more genetically distant conspecifics, consistent with negative iDD; Inga marginata exhibited positive iDD; five species exhibited no pattern. These findings demonstrate that genotype-specific plant–soil interactions can generate biologically relevant but variable impacts on seedling responses. This highlights the need to further investigate the drivers and ecological consequences of intraspecific genetic variation in plant–soil interactions and iDD in tropical forests.

title: Research Progress on Chinese Medicine Derived Bioactive Monomers in Breast Cancer Resistance and Programmed Cell Death
abstractText: Therapeutic responses in breast cancer are jointly shaped by molecular subtype, clonal evolution, and the tumor microenvironment. Endocrine therapy, chemotherapy, radiotherapy, and targeted therapy can all select for acquired resistance. Bioactive monomers derived from Chinese medicinal materials have defined chemical structures and frequently act on interconnected signaling networks. They may influence drug efflux, epithelial-mesenchymal transition, tumor stemness, and cell-death thresholds by modulating PI3K/AKT/mTOR, MAPK, NF-kappaB, AMPK/HIF-1alpha, and Wnt/beta-catenin signaling. This review evaluates representative compounds, including curcumin, shikonin, baicalin, baicalein, berberine, resveratrol, tanshinone IIA, and dihydroartemisinin, with emphasis on apoptosis, ferroptosis, necroptosis, autophagy-related processes, and restoration of treatment sensitivity. It further examines microenvironmental barriers formed by hypoxia, cancer-associated fibroblasts, tumor-associated macrophages, regulatory T cells, and immune checkpoints. Preclinical studies of shikonin-induced immunogenic cell death, berberine-mediated GSDME pyroptosis, and natural-polyphenol combinations that reshape immune infiltration provide a mechanistic bridge to immunotherapy; however, they do not establish these compounds as substitutes for, or routine partners of, immune-checkpoint inhibitors. Most evidence derives from cell lines and animal models, and opposite effects may occur with different doses, formulations, or treatment schedules. Future work should establish target causality in subtype-defined patient-derived models, quantify pharmacologic synergy, match experimental exposure to achievable human exposure, and use rigorously designed clinical trials to define the population likely to benefit and the boundaries of safety

title: Ethical and evidential challenges in adolescent puberty blockade: why informed consent alone is not enough
abstractText: In this viewpoint, I examine evidential and ethical issues regarding the use of puberty blockers for adolescent gender dysphoria, and analyse whether informed consent is functionally equipped to provide a legal and ethical justification for their use under conditions of clinical uncertainty. My normative analysis uses Beauchamp and Childress’ framework of respect for autonomy, beneficence, non maleficence and justice to examine the informed consent model in light of current evidence regarding benefits, risks, capacity and voluntariness. I identify five interacting factors that arguably undermine valid consent: diagnostic uncertainty and limited differential diagnosis; very low certainty evidence of benefit; uncertainty regarding potentially serious or irreversible harms; developmental limitations in decision making capacity; and compromised voluntariness due to social and emotional pressures. I argue that, taken together, these factors require an unusually strong conception of autonomy to over-ride beneficence and non maleficence in paediatric care. While informed consent remains necessary, I suggest that it is insufficient as the primary ethical or legal justification for adolescent puberty blocker treatment and that additional safeguards and justifications are required.

title: Integrative systematics reveal an unusual species of pedunculate ground beetles lacking fossorial legs from Late Cretaceous Kachin amber (Coleoptera: Carabidae: Scaritinae)
abstractText: Context The subfamily Scaritinae (Coleoptera: Carabidae) is a speciose, cosmopolitan group of ground beetles characterised by a pedunculate body form and modified fossorial forelegs, adaptations associated with a burrowing lifestyle in soil or sandy substrates. The fossil record of Scaritinae is scarce and only one Mesozoic species has been described up to the present. Aims A new genus and species of scaritine ground beetles is described from Late Cretaceous amber in northern Myanmar. Its phylogenetic relationship with extant lineages of Scaritinae was investigated and divergence times among lineages of Scaritinae were estimated. Its palaeoecology is also discussed from the perspective of morphological adaptation. Taxon A Late Cretaceous pedunculate ground beetle (Insecta: Coleoptera: Carabidae: Scaritinae), Cretoscarites burmanicus gen. et sp. nov., aligns well with extant Scaritinae, yet it lacks the fossorial legs typically seen in modern scaritines. Methods Its relationship with extant Scaritinae was investigated based on two datasets using maximum parsimony, Bayesian inference and maximum likelihood: (i) 55 morphological characters belonging to 16 taxa (representing 6 of the 7 tribes and 13 of the 20 subtribes of modern Scaritinae); and (ii) a combined morphological and molecular dataset for 16 taxa, comprising a partitioned alignment of 2772 bp from COI and 18S sequences of seven taxa, representing 5 tribes and 6 subtribes. Divergence times within Scaritinae were estimated in a Bayesian tip-dating framework based on both datasets under a relaxed clock. Key results Phylogenetic analyses using various approaches and datasets consistently placed Cretoscarites burmanicus within Scaritini. Among Scaritini, the nominal subtribe was recovered as the most likely closest relative of Cretoscarites burmanicus. Results indicate that Scaritinae originated in the Middle Jurassic (ca. 167–168 Mya) and the major lineages started to differentiate during the Cretaceous. The overall body form and small eye size suggest that it was likely a nocturnal, olfactory-tactile hunter inhabiting restricted or confined environments, whereas its simple, unmodified forelegs indicate a non-fossorial lifestyle. Conclusions The newly described scaritine ground beetle from Kachin amber can be confidently assigned to Scaritini based on our integrative phylogenetic approach. This finding represents the oldest documented occurrence (ca. 99 Mya) of this tribe to date and its unique forelegs suggest that the lifestyles of Scaritinae may have been more diverse in their early evolution than they are today. title: Capsaicin suppresses microglial inflammation through TRPV1–SSR4 interaction
abstractText: Abstract Background Transient receptor potential vanilloid 1 (TRPV1) is increasingly recognized as an important regulator of microglial response during neuroinflammation, a key pathological feature of various neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer’s disease. Capsaicin, the primary pungent component in chili peppers, executes its anti-inflammatory properties as a TRPV1 agonist. Although the mechanism of TRPV1 channel activation and signal transduction by capsaicin has been extensively studied, the protein–protein interaction-based mechanisms by which TRPV1 modulates microglial inflammatory responses in the context of neurodegeneration remains unclear. Methods We used a lipopolysaccharide-induced acute neuroinflammation model to examine the effects of TRPV1 activation and pharmacological blockade of TRPV1 channel gating on microglial inflammatory responses. Proximity labeling-based proteomics, bioluminescence resonance energy transfer, and NanoLuc Binary Technology were used to identify and characterize TRPV1-interacting proteins. Signal sequence receptor subunit 4 (SSR4) knockdown and forced interaction between TRPV1 and SSR4 were performed to assess the functional contribution of the TRPV1–SSR4 interaction. Structural modeling, BRET-based domain mapping, and colocalization analyses were further used to examine the molecular and subcellular features of SSR4 recruitment by TRPV1. Results In the neuroinflammatory model, the TRPV1 agonist capsaicin attenuated pro-inflammatory cytokine production, neuronal apoptosis, microgliosis, and microglial soma enlargement in a TRPV1-dependent manner. Notably, pharmacological blockade of TRPV1 channel gating by capsazepine did not abolish the anti-inflammatory action of capsaicin, suggesting an alternative mechanism of action beyond the canonical ligand-gated Ca 2 ⁺ influx. Screening of TRPV1 prey proteins and validation strategy identified SSR4 as a capsaicin-responsive, TRPV1-associated protein. SSR4 knockdown in microglia significantly diminished the suppression of inflammatory responses caused by TRPV1 activation. Conversely, forced interaction between TRPV1 and SSR4 partially mimicked the anti-inflammatory effects of TRPV1 activation. Further structural and cellular analyses suggested that the transmembrane region of TRPV1 supports SSR4 recruitment. Conclusions Our findings suggest that capsaicin suppresses microglial inflammation mediated by the TRPV1–SSR4 interaction, providing new insights into the chemical biology basis of TRPV1 interoceptive signaling and potential applications of natural TRPV1 agonists for modifying therapy of neuroinflammation-associated neurodegeneration.

Interaction between Yin-Yang vortex states and topological edge states in UTe 2
abstractText: Abstract UTe 2 , a strong candidate for spin-triplet superconductivity, hosts novel step-edge states and Yin-Yang vortices on its (011) surface, both of which are intimately connected to topological surface states. However, the interaction between these two types of states remains unexplored. Here, we use scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy (STM/STS) to investigate the coupling between step-edge states and Yin-Yang vortex states in UTe 2 . We uncover pronounced edge-vortex interactions, and find that the resulting in-gap spectral reconstruction is spatially asymmetric and depends sensitively on the position of the step edge relative to the vortex. Most strikingly, when the Yang vortex directly coincides with the step edge, the zero-energy conductance peak, a candidate Majorana mode signal, is locally suppressed. Our findings reveal an unexplored interplay between topological boundary states and vortex bound states in a spin-triplet superconductor, and establish step edges as a local tuning factor for vortex zero modes, providing possibilities for spatially selective manipulation of candidate Majorana modes through engineered boundary geometries.

Unpacking the teaching–research nexus: a phenomenographic analysis of student experiences in a medical university
abstractText: Abstract Background The integration of research and teaching in higher education has been widely discussed, with growing emphasis on fostering research-based learning environments. Within medical and health professions education, this integration is particularly critical, as research literacy and evidence‑based practice form core professional competencies. The concept of the teaching–research nexus posits that research-active faculty enhance student learning by introducing current knowledge and inquiry-based practices into the classroom. This not only deepens students’ subject understanding but also cultivates critical thinking and problem-solving skills. Despite its significance, there is a lack of studies exploring students’ perceptions of this nexus. This study addresses the identified need for qualitative insights and aims to explore what students understand as research and how the teaching–research nexus is enacted in their educational context. Methods A phenomenographic design was employed to investigate students’ conceptions of research and how the teaching-research nexus is enacted in their educational context. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 20 students from five academic programmes: Twelve enrolled in first-cycle health professions degrees and 8 in international master’s programmes in non-clinical disciplines. The analysis followed Dahlgren and Fallsberg’s seven steps of phenomenographic analysis. Results Analysis resulted in four distinct categories of understanding research, presented in an order that reflects increasing complexity: (1) “Research is a spark of curiosity,” (2) “Research is exploring a knowledge gap,” (3) “Research is examining and providing new knowledge,” and (4) “Research is a continuous practice.” These categories were structured along three themes of expanding awareness: students’ own engagement with research, their perceptions of faculty as research-active educators, and the nature of teaching and learning activities. Together, these elements form the study’s outcome space, illustrating variation in students’ understandings, from passive exposure to active, reflective engagement in research-informed learning. Conclusions Findings suggest that aligning pedagogical strategies with students’ current understanding of research can facilitate their transition from passive recipients to active participants in research. Faculty members play a pivotal role as scholarly role models, shaping students’ academic identity and reinforcing the dynamic nature of the teaching–research nexus.

title: One-Pot Green Synthesis of Low-Viscosity Acetal Epoxy Resins for Diluent-Free Industrial Processing and Closed-Loop Recycling of Carbon Fiber Composites
abstractText: Abstract Recyclable epoxy thermosets and their carbon fiber-reinforced polymer composites (CFRPs) have faced three long-standing bottlenecks: complex synthesis and purification processes, inherently high viscosity incompatible with the industrial vacuum-assisted resin infusion (VARI) process—the dominant technology for manufacturing large wind turbine blades and aerospace composites—and incomplete recovery of individual composite constituents. While dynamic covalent bonds offer a promising route to epoxy recyclability, most existing recyclable epoxy systems fail to simultaneously overcome these hurdles. Herein, we report a green, scalable one-pot synthesis of a novel low-viscosity acetal epoxy resin (BCAE) that simultaneously addresses the synthesis, processing, and end-of-life recycling challenges of epoxy thermosets. This telescoped protocol eliminates intermediate purification steps, delivering BCAE with an ultra-low viscosity of 1.9 Pa·s at 25 °C—6.7-fold lower than commercial bisphenol A diglycidyl ether (DGEBA)—enabling diluent-free VARI fabrication of high-performance CFRPs. The cured BCAE networks exhibit dual recyclability: catalyst-free thermal reprocessability and mild acid-triggered degradation under ambient conditions. Most notably, we demonstrate a closed-loop monomer recycling combined with an open-loop upcycling system with key quantitative breakthroughs: carbon fibers are recovered with 96.7% strength retention in the regenerated composite, the benzaldehyde monomer is recycled to resynthesize BCAE with identical performance, and the tertiary amine polyol degradation product is upcycled as a high-value curing agent for commercial epoxies. Life cycle assessment confirms that closed‑loop recycling reduces CO2‑equivalent emissions by approximately 79% compared with incineration. This work provides a general and industrially viable strategy for sustainable thermoset composites, aligning perfectly with global carbon neutrality goals.

title: Prevalence of frailty syndrome among patients with severe aortic stenosis qualified for TAVI
abstractText: Abstract Background Frailty syndrome is a common comorbidity in elderly patients with severe aortic stenosis (AS), significantly influencing outcomes of transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). Early identification of frailty and its determinants is essential for optimizing care and improving quality of life. Methods This cross-sectional, observational study included 113 Polish patients qualified for TAVI between January and September 2024. Frailty was assessed using the Tilburg Frailty Indicator (TFI). Quality of life, mental health, and social support were evaluated with TASQ, HADS, and MSPSS questionnaires. Logistic regression was used to identify predictors of frailty. Results Frailty syndrome was present in 82.3% of patients. Higher frailty levels were associated with worse NYHA class, unhealthy lifestyle, and increased emotional burden. Depression and anxiety were significantly correlated with frailty, especially its psychological domain. Logistic regression revealed that NYHA class, emotional impact (TASQ), and unhealthy lifestyle were independent predictors of frailty. Social support negatively correlated with social frailty scores, suggesting a protective effect. Conclusions Frailty is highly prevalent among patients with severe AS undergoing TAVI. Comprehensive preprocedural assessment should include physical, emotional, and social factors. Targeted interventions - particularly prehabilitation and psychosocial support - may help address modifiable components of frailty in this population. Clinical trial number Not applicable.

title: Solvent-Free Synthesis of Highly Luminescent Solid-State Boric Acid-Assisted Carbon Dots for Stable and High-Contrast Latent Fingerprint Visualization
abstractText: Abstract The development of efficient, stable, and environmentally friendly fluorescent materials for latent fingerprint visualization remains a major challenge in forensic science. Carbon dots (CDs) have emerged as promising fluorescent nanomaterials owing to their low toxicity, tunable optical properties, and eco-friendly nature. However, their practical application in solid-state systems is often hindered by aggregation-induced quenching (AIQ), which can significantly suppress fluorescence emission. In this study, highly luminescent boric acid-assisted carbon dots (B-CDs) were synthesized through a simple, rapid, and solvent-free thermal process using citric acid, urea, and boric acid as precursors. Unlike conventional approaches, the developed method enables the direct formation of solid-state emissive carbon dot powders without requiring additional surface passivation, purification, or polymeric matrices. Structural and spectroscopic characterizations supported the successful formation of heteroatom-functionalized B-CDs that exhibit excitation-dependent photoluminescence and strong solid-state emission. The synthesized B-CDs exhibited a high solid-state photoluminescence quantum yield of 77.5%. The B-CDs showed strong short-term stability, retaining more than 95% of their initial PL intensity after 60 min exposure to 95% relative humidity and during short-term thermal treatment up to 90 °C. Long-term measurements showed approximately 57% PL retention after 5 days at 95% relative humidity and approximately 48% after 5 days of thermal aging at 50 °C, while approximately 92% of the initial PL intensity was retained after 5 days of continuous UV irradiation. The proposed solvent-free synthesis strategy offers a simple and potentially scalable route for producing strongly emissive solid-state carbon dots, highlighting their potential for latent fingerprint visualization.

Pressure Control based Hybrid MPC and PID Control for Parallel Centrifugal Well Injection Pumps
abstractText: Well Injection pumps is essential equipment in the upstream oil and gas industry. These pumps are primarily employed to inject water into the reservoir to maintain reservoir pressure, or to waste the water excess after exploration. The most common use Pressure control is only PID control, which has limitations such as Complex and Time-Consuming Parameter Tuning and Poor Adaptability to Parameter Changes. To address this challenge, this study develops hybrid MPC and PID control for pressure control to increase response time and reduce overshoot due to parameter changes. To get the plant model, ARMAX (Auto Regressive Exogenous Moving Average with Exogenous Inputs) is used by analyzing historical measurement data for pressure and throttle valve. The proposed strategy effectively combines the fast response of the PID controller with the foresight and optimization capabilities of the MPC. Load change simulations show that the Hybrid MPC-PID controller exhibits faster response time and more precise overshoot reduction capability compared to the single PID and pure MPC strategies. The final optimized model achieved substantial improvements in the IAE index, where the hybrid MPC-PID achieved 0.37% compared to 4.71% for the pure MPC and 7.24% for the PID controller. The implementation of this Control enables increased efficiency in the Water Injection Pump.

Carbon Source Substitution During Submerged Fermentation Alters Cordyceps militaris Extracellular Vesicle Metabolite Profiles and Anti-Photoaging Activity
abstractText: Abstract Background: Cordyceps militaris extracellular vesicle-enriched preparations, operationally designated CMEVs in this study, are being explored as food-derived nanomaterials, but the effects of source material, fermentation stage, and carbon source on their characteristics and biological activity remain unclear. We compared CMEVs obtained from fruiting bodies and submerged liquid fermentation, selected a collection time, and examined the effects of four carbon sources on CMEV characteristics and protection against UVB-induced injury.Results: Compared with fruiting body-derived CMEVs, fermentation-derived CMEVs yielded more BCA-detectable protein per gram of source dry mass, had a more negative zeta potential, and showed a narrower particle-size distribution. In UVB-damaged HaCaT cells, fermentation-derived CMEVs resulted in higher cell viability, lower MMP1 and IL6 expression, and higher COL1A2 expression. The two source groups had similar particle-to-protein ratios. Although the BCA-measured protein concentration was highest on fermentation day 5, CMEVs collected on day 4 had a higher particle-to-protein ratio and a more uniform particle-size distribution. Day 4 was therefore selected for the subsequent experiments. Tre-CMEVs and Glc-CMEVs had similar protein concentrations, particle-to-protein ratios, and zeta potentials, while Tre-CMEVs showed a relatively narrow particle-size distribution. In UVB-damaged HaCaT cells, Tre-CMEVs reduced ROS and MDA, decreased IL6 and MMP1 expression, and increased COL1A2 expression. Tre-CMEVs also reduced wrinkle formation, epidermal thickening, lipid peroxidation, inflammation, and collagen loss in UVB-exposed mice. Untargeted metabolomics distinguished Tre-CMEVs from Glc-CMEVs and identified differential features related to amino acid and energy metabolism, including signals putatively annotated as arginine, glutamate, and tricarboxylic acid-cycle intermediates.Conclusions: Day 4 was selected as the collection point based on particle characteristics and cellular activity. Tre-CMEVs reduced oxidative stress, inflammatory responses, and matrix damage in HaCaT cells and alleviated UVB-induced skin injury in mice. These findings support further evaluation of Tre-CMEVs as a UVB-protective preparation.

The impact of electronic medical records on the quality of care: a scoping review.
abstractText: Electronic medical records (EMRs) have become an integral component of modern healthcare systems, with the potential to improve the quality, safety, and efficiency of healthcare delivery. This review aimed to evaluate the impact of EMR applications in healthcare systems based on the quality of care. A scoping review was conducted using three electronic databases (Web of Science, PubMed, and Scopus) from January 2015 to December 2019. The inclusion were open-access articles written in English, with quantitative and qualitative study designs. A total of 220 articles were retrieved from the literature search; 19 articles met the inclusion criteria and were eligible for the final analysis. The review identified five major quality-of-care domains, namely safe, effective, patient-centred, timely, and efficient. There were heterogeneous findings with some studies pointing toward positive, negative, or neutral consequences of EMR implementation in healthcare systems. This review suggests several vital future directions to further enhance the positive impacts of EMR in providing the best services to patients. Thus, recommendations focus on strengthening technical resources by addressing cost, ensuring the availability of appropriate software and support systems, and enhancing the comprehensiveness of user training.

title: Penicillin-resistant beta-haemolytic Group B Streptococcus isolated from a urinary tract infection in a non-pregnant adult
abstractText: Streptococcus agalactiae (Group B Streptococcus, GBS) is an established cause of urinary tract infections (UTIs) and is typically susceptible to penicillin. However, although rare, resistance to beta-lactam antibiotics is increasingly reported and may complicate treatment in adults. Early identification of resistant strains is essential to guide appropriate antimicrobial therapy. We report a case of a 54-year-old non-pregnant woman with diabetes mellitus (DM) who presented with symptomatic UTI. Urine culture yielded beta-haemolytic GBS at >10⁵ CFU/mL. Initial empirical treatment with amoxicillin-clavulanate was ineffective. Antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST) demonstrated resistance to penicillin. The isolate was identified as S. agalactiae by matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionisation time-of-flight mass spectrometry (MALDI-TOF MS), and susceptibility testing was performed in accordance with the latest Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute (CLSI) guidelines. Following the susceptibility results, therapy was switched to intravenous ceftriaxone, resulting in complete clinical resolution of symptoms. This case highlights the clinical importance of emerging beta-lactam resistance in GBS urinary infections in non-pregnant adults and emphasises the significance of culture-directed therapy. Although phenotypic resistance was confirmed, the absence of molecular characterisation warrants cautious interpretation given the rarity of penicillin-resistant GBS. Continued surveillance is necessary to monitor resistance trends and guide treatment strategies.
