Room temperature NO2 sensing in bottom gate WO3 thin film transistors: Ag versus Pd source/drain contacts and the inverse correlation between transistor and sensing performance
abstractText: Abstract Metal oxide Thin Film Transistors (TFTs) are promising candidates for next-generation gas sensors as they combine gas detection with built-in signal amplification. However, it is still not confirmed whether better transistor performance will always lead to better gas sensing performance. In this work, two Bottom Gate Tungsten Trioxide (WO 3 ) TFTs with different source/drain contact metals, silver (Ag) and palladium (Pd), referred as BG TFT-1 and BG TFT-2 respectively are fabricated by RF sputtering, material (SEM, XRD) and electrical characterizations-(I D -V D ), transfer (I D -V G ), capacitance–frequency (C–f), and capacitance–gate voltage (C–V G ) measurements done. TFT parameters- transconductance (g m ), I ON /I OFF ratio, threshold voltage (V TH ), sub-threshold swing (SS), and mobility (µ FE ) were determined to assess charge transport, gate modulation, dielectric behaviour and interface quality. Later, they were systematically investigated for NO 2 sensing for concentrations ranging from 0.1 to 10 ppm at room temperature. The WO 3 thin film exhibited a monoclinic crystal structure with a preferred (002) orientation and an average crystallite size of 9.7 nm. Both TFTs showed stable transistor operation and reversible sensing behaviour toward NO 2 . Although BG TFT-2 exhibited superior electrical performance, including higher field effect mobility (µ FE = 8.6 × 10 −3 cm 2 V −1 s −1 ), higher transconductance and a larger I ON /I OFF ratio, BG TFT-1 consistently produced a stronger sensing response. At 10 ppm NO 2 , BG TFT-1 achieved a maximum response of 99.2% with a response time of 28 s, whereas BG TFT-2 showed a response of 96.0% with a response time of 32 s. The enhanced sensing performance of BG TFT-1 is attributed to its higher threshold voltage (V TH ) and lower initial carrier concentration, which allow NO 2 adsorption to produce a larger change in channel current. These findings demonstrate that electrical performance alone does not determine gas sensing performance. Instead, the properties of the metal–semiconductor interface and the channel surface may play a more important role in determining sensor response. This study highlights WO 3 TFTs with Bottom Gate configuration as promising low-power, room temperature NO 2 sensors that are compatible with future integrated sensing technologies.

title: Clinical and Serological Evaluation and Management of Rheumatic Disease-Associated Interstitial Lung Disease
abstractText: In 2011, the American Thoracic Society (ATS) recommended that antibody testing be included in the evaluation of patients with interstitial lung disease (ILD) to assess for an underlying connective tissue disease, particularly in cases of lingering diagnostic uncertainty, such as differentiating ILD from idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.¹ Specifically, the ATS endorsed routine testing for antinuclear antibodies (ANA), rheumatoid factor (RF), and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide (anti CCP) antibodies. However, autoantibody testing in isolation is rarely diagnostic and results must be interpreted within a clinical context. Accordingly, the interpretation of autoantibody testing and its implications for the diagnosis and management of rheumatic disease-associated ILD remain central to optimizing care in this patient population. Serology testing is best utilized as an adjunct rather than a standalone diagnostic tool. Over reliance on antibody results without clinical correlation can result in misdiagnosis and inappropriate treatment. It is therefore important to integrate serologic data into the broader diagnostic workup of systemic autoimmune rheumatic disease-associated ILD.

BioSIFTR: functional inference from shallow shotgun sequencing using biome-specific genome catalogues benchmarked in gut microbiomes
abstractText: Abstract Shallow shotgun sequencing is an accurate microbiome profiling method, but its use for functions is limited. BioSIFTR extrapolates shallow shotgun read mapping to precalculated pangenome functions in 15 MGnify biome-specific catalogues, which span host-associated and environmental microbiomes. We benchmarked BioSIFTR on synthetic communities and on three gut microbiomes — red junglefowl, mouse, and human — using matched deep shotgun and 16S rRNA metabarcoding data, outperforming similar approaches. Further validation will require matched benchmark datasets and is a priority for future work. BioSIFTR is thus a practical method for functional inference from cost-effective shallow shotgun sequencing, currently validated in gut microbiomes.

title: Evaluation of Context, Input, Process, and Product Models of Islamic Religious Character Development Programs
abstractText: This study aims to evaluate the Islamic Religious Character Development Program using the Context, Input, Process, and Product (CIPP) model in Al Falah Elementary School, Surabaya, and Khadijah Elementary School, Surabaya. This qualitative study employed a multisite design. The research data comprised information on the context, input, process, and product of the program, obtained through in-depth interviews, participatory observations, and documentation involving principals, teachers, students, and relevant stakeholders. Data were analyzed using an interactive model of data condensation, data display, and conclusion drawing and verification, followed by within-site and cross-site analysis. The findings show that the programs were developed based on students' needs and institutional directions, supported by human resources, curriculum, program instruments, facilities, and stakeholder involvement. Implementation involved habituation, role modeling, mentoring, monitoring, and evaluation. Program products were reflected in religious practices, Qur'anic literacy and memorization, moral conduct, manners, discipline, responsibility, independence, and care for others. Observation and documentation indices reached 100% across all CIPP components, indicating strong supporting evidence rather than 100% program success. Sustainable character development requires continuous program improvement and stronger school–family collaboration.

The Importance of Technology in Recording and Preserving Oral Literature: Evidence from the Sukuma Community of Usagara, Misungwi District, Mwanza Region
abstractText: This article examines how digital technology has transformed the recording, preservation, and dissemination of oral literature within the Sukuma community of Usagara Ward in Misungwi District, Mwanza Region, Tanzania. The study was guided by the Diffusion of Innovation Theory and employed a qualitative research approach supported by descriptive design. Data were collected from a sample of 45 participants, including oral artists, teachers, students, cultural practitioners, and community elders, selected through purposive and snowball sampling techniques. Primary data were obtained through semi-structured interviews, focus group discussions, and observation, while thematic analysis was used to interpret the findings. Trustworthiness was ensured through triangulation and member checking, while ethical considerations such as informed consent and confidentiality were strictly observed.Findings reveal that digital technologies such as mobile phones, audio recorders, video cameras, radio, television, and online platforms have significantly improved the preservation and accessibility of oral literature, with 84.4% of participants acknowledging their effectiveness in safeguarding oral traditions. The study further shows that digital tools enhance teaching and learning (68.9%), expand dissemination beyond local boundaries (77.8%), and strengthen cultural continuity (71.1%). However, 60% of participants expressed concerns regarding the loss of authenticity, reduced communal participation, and the transformation of oral performance dynamics in digitally mediated contexts. Despite these challenges, technology is widely perceived as a powerful tool for cultural preservation when appropriately applied.The article concludes that digital technology plays a dual role in both preserving and transforming oral literature, creating new opportunities for documentation, education, and global visibility while also introducing tensions related to authenticity and cultural integrity. It recommends strengthening community-based digital literacy, establishing structured oral literature archives, and developing cultural policies that protect indigenous intellectual property while promoting sustainable digital preservation practices.

title: Analyzing Neural Responses to Video Advertisements: From Visual Attention to Cognitive Load
abstractText: Understanding consumer engagement is essential for optimizing marketing strategies. This study analyzes neural responses using electroencephalography (EEG) to distinguish interesting and ordinary video advertisements. EEG data from 30 participants (aged 17–40) were recorded across eight channels (F8, F7, T8, T7, P8, P7, O2, O1) and decomposed into five subbands (Delta, Theta, Alpha, Beta, Gamma). Key features, including Power Spectral Density (PSD), Mean Absolute Value (MAV), Hjorth Activity, Zero Crossing Rate (ZCR), and Wavelet Transform, were extracted and analyzed. Results showed that Gamma activity in occipital regions (O1, O2) was higher during interesting advertisements, indicating heightened visual attention, and reduced Beta activity in frontal regions (F7, F8) indicating reduced cognitive load. These findings offer valuable insights for neuromarketing by identifying neural markers of engagement and providing actionable insights for designing effective advertisements.

title: The present does not reflect the past: geographic mismatches between fossil and modern records are widespread across the tree of life
abstractText: Abstract The distribution of organisms across Earth provides insight into the origin and maintenance of biodiversity. Abundant fossil evidence suggests taxa have undergone substantial range changes over time. However, biogeographic theory and models often tend to assume that clades originated in the regions where we observe them today. Understanding the prevalence of geographically dynamic clades across the tree of life provides a way to evaluate these assumptions, thereby refining key evolutionary hypotheses. We provide a review of such range-shifting clades using a two-pronged approach. First, literature searches uncovered examples across most major multicellular groups (comprising 129 clades with mismatches between fossil and modern ranges). Concurrently, we used the well-sampled mammalian fossil record as a case study, finding that more than half of its terrestrial families (51%) had substantial (>1000 km) geographic mismatches. Geographically dynamic lineages are both common and widespread, but despite their ubiquity, fossil–modern mismatches have only recently been integrated into phylogenetic and biogeographic methods and no comprehensive overview of their advantages and challenges exists. We therefore review the current state of the field and discuss case studies where fossil evidence reshaped prevailing biogeographic theory. Biogeographers must take advantage of these rich fossil histories to better elucidate evolutionary theory across space and time.

title: Quality assessment of exercise videos for chronic diseases on social media platforms: a systematic review and meta-analysis
abstractText: Abstract Background Social media platforms have become important sources of exercise information for people with chronic diseases, but the evidence on the quality of such videos has never been quantitatively synthesized. This study aimed to evaluate the educational quality of exercise videos for chronic disease populations on social media and to examine how video characteristics, engagement metrics and uploader type relate to that quality. Methods A systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted following PRISMA guidelines. Seven sources (Web of Science, PubMed, SportDiscus (EBSCO), Embase, Scopus, CNKI and Google Scholar) were searched from inception to September 2025; eligibility was restricted to English- and Chinese-language studies assessing the quality of exercise videos for chronic disease management on social media. Two reviewers independently screened and extracted data. Study-level random-effects meta-analyses (restricted maximum likelihood) were performed in Stata 19 (SE), reporting 95% confidence intervals (CI) and, for the principal instruments, 95% prediction intervals (PI); quality strata were compared by meta-regression. Study quality was appraised with the eight-item D’Souza framework. Results Seventeen studies comprising 1,515 videos were included; 13 (76.5%) were conducted in Turkey, and YouTube was the dominant platform (16/17, 94.1%). Overall quality was low to moderate. Pooled mean scores were 2.96 of 5 for the Global Quality Scale (95% CI 2.63–3.29; 95% PI 1.70–4.23), 2.53 of 5 for the modified DISCERN (95% CI 2.18–2.90; 95% PI 1.24–3.84) and 1.49 of 4 for the JAMA benchmark criteria (95% CI 0.65–2.33), with substantial heterogeneity (I² 93.0–98.6%). Video duration, view count, likes, dislikes and comments did not differ across quality strata. Videos from individual physician accounts were over-represented in the poor-quality stratum (34.2% versus 3.6% in the good stratum, p = 0.03), whereas those from academic or institutional channels were more often of good quality ( p = 0.068). Conclusion Exercise videos for chronic disease populations are widely available but of suboptimal educational quality, and engagement metrics do not indicate quality. Higher-quality content is associated with academic and institutional channels rather than individual physician accounts. These conclusions rest on English- and Chinese-language, largely Turkish and YouTube-based evidence, and the wide prediction intervals warrant caution in generalizing them. title: Dynamic facial movements shape how confident speakers appear
abstractText: Abstract Human communication is inherently multimodal, relying on signals conveyed through speech, vocal tone and facial movements. While gestures and vocal cues are known to influence how speech is understood, the role of facial movements remains poorly specified. Here, we test whether dynamic facial movements shape how spoken responses are interpreted by systematically modulating listener inferences of speaker confidence and doubt. Using a data-driven reverse-correlation approach and a generative model of facial behaviour, we manipulated speakers’ upper-face movements while holding verbal content constant. On each trial, participants (n = 44; UK English and Mandarin Chinese speakers) rated the confidence of speakers responding to questions (e.g. ‘Would they make a good leader?’) on a five-point scale across 1800 trials. We find that opposing facial movements bias these inferences: eye closure and brow raising are associated with confidence, whereas brow lowering and eye tightening are associated with doubt. Signal amplitude further shapes these inferences, primarily by intensifying perceived doubt for doubt-associated movements. These mappings are largely shared between the two cultural groups, indicating common signal–inference relationships alongside differences in the weighting of specific cues. Together, these findings show that facial movements provide graded social signals that systematically shape how spoken responses are interpreted.

Short-Term Reservoir Inflow Prediction Using Weather Forecast Data and ExtraTrees Regressor for Hydroelectric Power Plant Operations
abstractText: Reliable short-term inflow forecasting is critical for optimizing hydroelectric power plant (HPP) operations, where water availability is directly influenced by dynamic and often extreme weather patterns. Inaccurate inflow estimations can result in either uncontrolled water spills or reservoir levels dropping below operational thresholds, both leading to reduced energy efficiency and potential operational risks. This study presents a data-driven inflow prediction framework utilizing the ExtraTrees Regressor algorithm, trained on four years of combined historical hydrological and meteorological data, and validated using independent weather forecast datasets. The model achieves a coefficient of determination (R²) of up to 82%, demonstrating strong predictive accuracy. By incorporating forecasted weather parameters into the predictive model, the proposed approach enables proactive reservoir management and more effective turbine scheduling, significantly reducing the incidence of emergency spill events. Findings from this research highlight the advantages of transitioning from conventional intuition-based methods to systematic data-driven strategies, offering enhanced reliability, operational resilience, and efficiency in hydropower generation planning.

title: A method for generating Verilog descriptions of FPGA control units based on Extended Petri Nets
abstractText: This paper proposes a method for constructing Verilog descriptions of control systems that include data operations, based on the Extended Interpreted Petri Nets (EIPN). In the proposed approach, external influences are considered within the structure of the Petri net through the introduction of several extensions, which provides a unified formalism for describing the states of a control system and firing conditions, and makes it possible to describe the control logic together with data. This method enables the synthesis of a synchronous Verilog description from an EIPN model without conversion into a finite-state machine. Rules are also proposed for representing the net places in a Verilog description depending on their boundedness. To correctly update the system state, a marking update mechanism is used. The operability of the method is demonstrated using the example of a liquid mixing process control system that includes parallel and synchronized processes. The proposed method extends the class of modeled systems, since the EIPN includes the class of k-bounded Petri nets and makes it possible to specify a set of actions when transitions fire.

title: Full vectorial maxwell equations with continuous angular indices—part II: numerical solvers and convergence analysis
abstractText: Abstract In part I of this work, we established an analytic framework for solving Maxwell's equations in spherical geometry with continuous angular indices (ℓ,m)∈R2, proving finite-energy conditions for singular solutions and formulating continuous spectral integrals in weighted Sobolev spaces. In this companion article (part II), we develop and validate numerical methods that operationalize this framework. We introduce a Galerkin discretization of the coupled angular operator on divergence-free continuous-index vector bases. To reconstruct physical fields, we complement this with an Eisenstein-type spectral integral, evaluated by mapped Gauss–Legendre quadrature. These methods explicitly account for non-orthogonality of the basis and the singular behaviour near the origin. The block formulation acts on the full matrix-valued angular Maxwell operator and is not restricted to the wedge and cone geometries used below as analytically tractable benchmarks. We analyse and numerically demonstrate convergence. The hybrid pipeline is validated by reproducing eigenmode frequencies of spherical cavities with wedge and cone modifications to within 1−2% of full-wave high-frequency structure simulator (HFSS) simulations. Together with part I, this paper completes a unified analytic–computational framework for singular electromagnetic fields with continuous angular indices.

title: A Patient-Centred Approach to Optimizing Inhaled Therapy: Integrating Patient, Device, Drug and Disease Factors
abstractText: Inhaled medications are crucial for the management of respiratory conditions such as chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and asthma, although their efficacy is contingent upon selecting the most appropriate inhaler and medication for each patient. Consideration should be given to factors such as inhaler technique, patient preference, coordination, inspiratory flow, small airway disease, and medication-related side effects. A patient-centred approach can maximize the benefits of inhaled therapy while minimizing potential risks.

title: Technology Meets Theology: Understanding AI-Driven Wellness in Muslim Prayer Apps
abstractText: Abstract This study examines the experiences and perceptions of Muslim users regarding the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in prayer apps and its impact on their religious and online communication activities. Through in-depth online interviews with a diverse group of participants, this study reveals that AI-driven prayer apps foster a sense of virtual community, bridging geographic distances, and enabling meaningful interactions among Muslims. AI tools like chatbots and reminders support emotional well-being by offering comfort, guidance, and companionship. Further, these tools increase religious awareness and empower users to customize their spiritual practices and access educational resources independently. However, perceptions of AI vary, with trust influenced by transparency, privacy concerns, and past experiences. This study emphasizes the importance of transparent and reliable AI tools to build user confidence. Lastly, the findings contribute to theories on digital religion and wellness, offering practical insights for developers, users, and religious organizations.

title: PENGARUH PROBLEM BASED LEARNING DAN KEDISIPLINAN BELAJAR TERHADAP KEMAMPUAN PEMECAHAN MASALAH MATEMATIKA SISWA SEKOLAH DASAR
abstractText: ABSTRACT Mathematical problem-solving is an essential competency that needs to be developed from elementary school; however, its development remains challenging, particularly in learning whole-number concepts. This study aimed to analyze the effects of the Problem Based Learning (PBL) model and learning discipline on students’ mathematical problem-solving ability, both partially and simultaneously. A quantitative approach with a quasi-experimental nonequivalent control group design was employed. The sample consisted of 68 fifth-grade students, comprising 38 students from SDN 7 Belinyu as the experimental group and 30 students from SDN 5 Belinyu as the control group. Data were collected through written pretests and posttests and a learning discipline questionnaire, then analyzed using the independent-samples t-test, Analysis of Covariance (ANCOVA), multiple linear regression, and N-Gain, with the assistance of SPSS 25. The results showed that the experimental group achieved a mean posttest score of 79.18, higher than the control group’s score of 63.63. This difference remained statistically significant after controlling for initial ability. Learning discipline was also positively and significantly associated with problem-solving ability. The regression model explained 60.8% of the variance in this ability. The experimental group’s N-Gain was 0.7621, categorized as high, whereas the control group’s N-Gain was 0.5872, categorized as moderate. These findings support the use of PBL as an alternative approach to mathematics instruction focused on problem-solving, while taking learning discipline and the limitations of the research design into account. ABSTRAK Kemampuan pemecahan masalah matematika merupakan kompetensi penting yang perlu dikembangkan sejak sekolah dasar, tetapi pembelajarannya masih menghadapi tantangan, terutama pada materi bilangan cacah. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis pengaruh model Problem Based Learning (PBL) dan kedisiplinan belajar terhadap kemampuan pemecahan masalah matematika siswa, baik secara parsial maupun simultan. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan desain quasi-experimental berbentuk nonequivalent control group design. Sampel terdiri atas 68 siswa kelas V, yaitu 38 siswa SDN 7 Belinyu sebagai kelompok eksperimen dan 30 siswa SDN 5 Belinyu sebagai kelompok kontrol. Data diperoleh melalui tes uraian pretest–posttest dan angket kedisiplinan belajar, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan uji independent-samples t-test, Analysis of Covariance (ANCOVA), regresi linear berganda, dan N-Gain dengan bantuan SPSS 25. Hasil menunjukkan bahwa rata-rata posttest kelompok eksperimen mencapai 79,18, lebih tinggi daripada kelompok kontrol sebesar 63,63. Perbedaan tersebut tetap signifikan setelah kemampuan awal dikendalikan. Kedisiplinan belajar juga berhubungan positif dan signifikan dengan kemampuan pemecahan masalah. Model regresi menjelaskan 60,8% variasi kemampuan tersebut. Nilai N-Gain kelompok eksperimen sebesar 0,7621 berkategori tinggi, sedangkan kelompok kontrol sebesar 0,5872 berkategori sedang. Temuan ini mendukung penggunaan PBL sebagai alternatif pembelajaran matematika yang berorientasi pada pemecahan masalah, dengan tetap memperhatikan kedisiplinan belajar dan keterbatasan desain penelitian.

The Fate of Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) in Municipal Solid Waste Incineration: Atmospheric Emissions from a Waste-to-Energy Plant
abstractText: Abstract The atmospheric fate of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) represents a very recent field of research. While ISO and CEN standards are yet under development, PFAS have been identified during the past years in atmospheric emissions, ambient air, and deposition. As high-quality field data are currently scarce, the objectives of this study were to (i) characterize atmospheric PFAS emissions of a state-of-the-art waste-to-energy (WtE) plant under representative operational conditions and (ii) evaluate the emission impact in ambient air in the vicinity of the plant. Results suggest a contribution from the WtE plant at the nearest ambient monitoring location, 450 m downwind of the plant, with a measurable contribution and distinct PFAS fingerprint closely matching the emission profiles independently characterized at two grate incinerator lines. Quantified PFAS emissions do not exceed the temporary assessment framework for ambient air in Flanders. Furthermore, optimization of the activated carbon (AC) dosage achieved a 95% reduction in emissions at line 1, with subsequent emission levels approaching those of field blanks. The waste treatment sector represents a critical frontier of environmental management. Building experimental evidence of potential PFAS releases will be key to ensure comprehensive strategies for responsible PFAS management in the years ahead.

Assessment of Candida attributes under in vitro repeated exposure to hydrogen peroxide
abstractText: Abstract Fungal infections have emerged as a significant concern in healthcare, due to the development of antifungal resistance and the limited availability of diagnostic and therapeutic options. The Candida species represent a category of particular importance with regard to fungi. Therefore, the implementation of infection prevention and control measures, such as hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) disinfection, is imperative in healthcare settings. In consideration of the existing literature, which demonstrates that repeated exposure to H 2 O 2 does not compromise microbial tolerance to the disinfectant, the expression of virulence attributes may be altered under the influence of external selective pressure. The present study aims to evaluate the effect of repeated exposure to H 2 O 2 on antifungal susceptibility profiles, catalase production, and biofilm formation on Candida strains in a phenotypic assessment of the microbial behaviour. In previous studies, strains of C. albicans , C. parapsilosis , and C. auris were repeatedly exposed to different H 2 O 2 concentrations and evaluated for their susceptibility to the disinfectant over 30 days. The present study demonstrated that repeated exposure to H₂O₂ resulted only in minor fluctuations of the antifungal susceptibility of C. albicans and C. parapsilosis , but not of C. auris . Repeated exposure to H₂O₂ demonstrated no variation in catalase production or alteration in biofilm formation for the evaluated species. In conclusion, repeated exposure to H₂O₂ resulted in only minor fluctuations in antifungal susceptibility in C. albicans and C. parapsilosis strains, demonstrating that utilization of H 2 O 2 as a daily disinfectant is safe in relation to microbial adaptation. However, environmental surveillance is advised to prevent the inadvertent development of antifungal resistance.

title: When High Engagement Masks Workplace Toxicity: The Moderating Role of Empathetic Leadership
abstractText: Background: This study introduces the concept of false positive engagement. Objective: This study examines the relationship between toxic workplace environment and employee engagement, as well as the buffering role of empathetic leadership in a high-risk state-owned energy construction sector in Indonesia. Despite increasing aggregate employee engagement scores, several engagement drivers such as work-life balance, communication, and recognition showed declining trends, indicating a potential false positive engagement phenomenon. Methods: Using a quantitative approach, data were collected from 181 employees of PT XYZ through an online questionnaire survey. The study employed Partial Least Squares-Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to test the proposed hypotheses and moderation model. Results: The findings reveal that toxic workplace environment significantly reduces employee engagement (β = -0.195; p = 0.001). Furthermore, empathetic leadership significantly weakens the negative effect of toxic workplace conditions on employee engagement (β = -0.122; p = 0.038). Conclusion: The study contributes to the organizational behavior and leadership literature by introducing the concept of false positive engagement and highlighting the importance of empathetic leadership as a psychological buffering mechanism in high-pressure project-based organizations. Practically, the findings suggest that organizations should not rely solely on aggregate engagement indices when evaluating workforce well-being and organizational health.

abstractText: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality, with prevalence projected to rise by nearly 25% between 2020 and 2050 to reach approximately 600 million people worldwide.1 COPD is characterized by persistent airflow limitation, leading to chronic dyspnea and reduced exercise capacity. Patients experience exacerbations of COPD (ECOPDs), clinically significant acute episodes characterized by increased airway inflammation and sudden worsening of breathlessness, which contribute substantially to lung function decline and are strongly associated with mortality.2 Exacerbations account for the vast majority of COPD-related healthcare use, driving hospital admissions, healthcare costs, long-term functional decline, and mortality risk.2 Despite progress in inhaled and biologic therapies, the management of recurrent exacerbations remains a significant challenge, and in fact, admissions for COPD are uniquely increasing rather than decreasing when compared with other chronic diseases after adjusting for population growth and aging in Canada.3 This highlights two important clinical realities: 1) that the current approach to COPD care is failing, and 2) that for both patients and health systems alike, there is a pressing need for innovative strategies to address and reduce the burden of COPD exacerbation admissions and readmissions.

title: Power Allocation Optimization In Hybrid Energy Storage System Based On Low Pass Filter And Artificial Neural Network
abstractText: This paper presents optimizing power allocation in hybrid energy storage systems (HESS) by combining Low Pass Filter (LPF) and Artificial Neural Network (ANN) techniques. Conventional LPF-based strategies employ fixed cut-off frequencies that cannot adapt to dynamic operating conditions, resulting in suboptimal performance and reduced battery lifespan. This research proposes optimization framework that determines optimal cut-off frequencies through three approaches: cost-based, stress-based, and hybrid optimization. Spectral analysis of requested power confirmed that energy content is predominantly concentrated in low-frequency ranges (10^-6 to 10^-3 Hz), justifying the frequency-based power allocation strategy. The hybrid optimization method yielded an optimal cut-off frequency of 0.0013 Hz, balancing economic and technical considerations with a 15% reduction in battery stress compared to cost-based approaches while increasing system costs by only 8%. The implemented ANN model achieved predictive capability (R² = 0.9728) in determining optimal cut-off frequencies across various operating conditions. Performance evaluations demonstrated that the ANN-based approach produces nearly identical power allocation patterns compared to conventional LPF methods while executing approximately 120 times faster, enabling real-time adaptation to changing system conditions. The combined methodology effectively separates low-frequency power components (87%) to batteries and high-frequency components (13%) to supercapacitors, optimizing component utilization based on their intrinsic characteristics while maintaining system efficiency above 88%.

Rapid turnover of sex chromosomes is associated with speciation in Neotropical armored catfish Harttia (Siluriformes, Loricariidae)
abstractText: Abstract Background The Neotropical armored catfish genus Harttia is an exceptional model for studying sex chromosome evolution, as it harbors the highest diversity of multiple sex chromosome systems known among fishes. However, the evolutionary history of these systems and their contribution to lineage diversification remain unresolved. We generated genome-wide DArTseq data for 17 Harttia species to investigate the origins of sex chromosome turnover, reconstruct phylogenetic and biogeographic history, identify sex-linked markers, and test whether multiple sex chromosomes are associated with increased speciation. Results Genome-wide SNP analyses resolved three major Harttia clades and dated their diversification to the last 10 million years, coinciding with major Neotropical drainage rearrangements. We identified 443 candidate sex-linked markers that suggest independent origins for the X₁X₂Y and XY₁Y₂ multiple sex chromosome systems. Ancestral chromosome-number reconstruction supported an ancestral karyotype of 2n = 58, while integration of candidate sex-linked markers with previous cytogenetic evidence is consistent with an ancestral homomorphic XY system followed by independent chromosome rearrangements generating multiple sex chromosomes in distinct lineages. State-dependent diversification analyses revealed significantly higher speciation rates in clades carrying multiple sex chromosomes than in those with simple systems, suggesting a close association between rapid sex chromosome turnover and lineage diversification. Conclusions Our results provide the first genome-wide evolutionary framework for Harttia , suggesting that multiple sex chromosome systems may be associated with elevated diversification in some Harttia lineages, while highlighting the need for broader genomic and taxonomic sampling to test this association. These findings identify Harttia as a powerful model for investigating how sex chromosome turnover, chromosome evolution, and landscape history jointly shape biodiversity.

title: Neurodivergence in medicine: strengths, challenges and workforce implications in Aotearoa New Zealand
abstractText: aims: Neurodivergence is increasingly recognised within healthcare workforces internationally yet remains largely absent from workforce policy and planning in Aotearoa New Zealand. This viewpoint argues that neurodivergence is not a challenge to be accommodated but a dimension of diversity with implications for workforce sustainability. methods: This viewpoint uses lived experience to motivate and illustrate an argument informed by a narrative review of international evidence on neurodivergence in medical education, clinical practice and workforce design. Policy frameworks are considered alongside current workforce pressures. results: Neurodivergent clinicians may contribute strengths in pattern recognition, lateral thinking and adaptability. However, standardised assessment frameworks, “masking” demands, disclosure risks and neurotypically designed workplaces create barriers to entry, progression and retention. Frameworks do not currently address cognitive diversity, representing both an equity gap and a missed opportunity during acute workforce shortages. This article introduces “cognitive infrastructure”—the design of systems, workflows and environments to support cognitive diversity—as a framing concept for workforce sustainability. conclusions: International evidence supports neurodiversity-informed approaches to workforce design. While local evidence remains limited, the New Zealand medical workforce shortages are sufficiently acute that incorporating neurodiversity and cognitive infrastructure into workforce planning, education design and leadership development represents a proportionate and evidence-aligned response.

Mapping Artificial Intelligence Research in Business and Management Higher Education: A Bibliometric Analysis
abstractText: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping business and management higher education, yet the field remains dispersed across educational, managerial, and technological conversations. This study maps that literature through a reproducible bibliometric review of Dimensions.ai records published from 2017 to 2025. The search and final export were completed on August 22, 2026. PRISMA 2020-guided screening retained 352 English-language open-access articles, chapters, and monographs. Descriptive indicators were combined with VOSviewer 1.6.20 analyses of co-authorship, contributor citations, cited-author co-citation, and title-and-abstract term co-occurrence. Annual output increased from 1 publication in 2017 to 191 in the complete 2025 publication year. Citation impact was concentrated in a small number of recent studies, while the co-authorship network remained fragmented into several small groups. Country results placed the United Kingdom first among records with affiliation metadata, although country information was missing for 182 of 352 records. After removing metadata artifacts, the most frequent title-and-abstract terms included intelligence, ChatGPT, business, opportunity, assessment, and engagement. The study contributes a transparent, multi-layer map of an emerging field and identifies priorities for curriculum design, assessment, responsible AI governance, and stronger cross-institutional collaboration.

Resolving GPCR Activation and Signaling Dynamics by Solution NMR Spectroscopy
abstractText: G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) are inherently dynamic transmembrane receptors that recognize various extracellular stimuli and mediate diverse signaling events. NMR spectroscopy is an important method to resolve the complex conformational energy landscapes of GPCRs and to probe the dynamic receptor-ligand/receptor-transducer interactions, which are critical in modulating functional diversity but are generally lacking in the static structures obtained by cryo-EM and X-ray crystallography studies. This review summarizes current advances in applying solution NMR to study GPCR structural dynamics during activation and signaling. We cover recent progress in sample preparation and isotopic labeling strategies, as well as critical NMR experimental methodologies that help illuminate transient interactions and functional intermediates. We then highlight representative studies that utilize the power of NMR to provide unique insights into GPCR signaling mechanisms that are difficult to access by other methods.

title: What predicts attainment of substantial clinical benefit in neck pain–related disability 24 months after surgery for cervical spondylotic myelopathy? A QOD CSM study
abstractText: OBJECTIVE Although surgery for cervical spondylotic myelopathy (CSM) has traditionally focused on halting neurological deterioration from myelopathy, many patients also report long-term improvements in neck pain and neck pain–related disability—outcomes not typically considered primary goals of intervention. This study aimed to identify preoperative predictors for attainment of substantial clinical benefit (SCB) in neck pain–related disability after CSM surgery. METHODS The authors retrospectively analyzed prospectively collected data from the 14 highest accruing Spine CORe™ sites in the Quality Outcomes Database CSM dataset. Logistic regression, XGBoost, and random forest models were trained to predict SCB attainment, defined as ≥ 20-point improvement in Neck Disability Index (NDI) score at 24 months postoperatively. Input features included demographic, clinical, and surgical variables in addition to baseline patient-reported outcomes. Model performance was evaluated via area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) analysis. RESULTS Of 1085 prospectively enrolled patients, 904 met the inclusion criteria for this analysis. The cohort had a mean age of 60.9 years, 48.3% were female, and 76.1% were White. The mean NDI score improved from 38.0 at baseline to 21.1 at 24 months, with 52.7% of patients achieving minimal clinically important difference and 44.7% achieving SCB. Significant positive predictors of SCB included higher baseline neck pain intensity (OR 1.99) and greater interference with recreation (OR 1.77), work (OR 1.57), lifting (OR 1.44), and driving (OR 1.36), as well as anterior surgical approach (OR 1.67) and higher socioeconomic status (SES) index (OR 1.23). Significant negative predictors included fusion stopping at C7 (OR 0.77) and Medicare, Medicaid, or government/Veterans Affairs (VA) insurance (OR 0.79). Logistic regression, XGBoost, and random forest models showed good discriminative performance (AUROC 0.78–0.82). CONCLUSIONS In a large prospective cohort of operative CSM patients, higher baseline neck pain intensity; greater interference with recreation, work, lifting, and driving; anterior surgical approach; and higher SES were associated with greater likelihood of achieving SCB for neck pain–related disability. Fusion stopping at C7 and Medicare, Medicaid, or government/VA insurance were negative predictors. This is the first study to identify factors predicting SCB in NDI score after CSM surgery, challenging traditional views on the effectiveness of surgery for relief from neck pain–related disability in this population and demonstrating that a subset of patients can achieve substantial, sustained relief. These results highlight the potential for data-driven approaches to enhance patient selection and optimize surgical decision-making in the treatment of CSM.

abstractText: This study aims to determine and analyze the effect of employee training and development on the implementation of quality management at PT Cipta Tenaga Nusantara, both partially and simultaneously. This study employed a quantitative approach using an associative research design. The research population consisted of employees of PT Cipta Tenaga Nusantara, with a sample of 60 respondents. The sampling technique used was purposive sampling, with the criteria that respondents must have worked for at least six months and understand the company's work procedures. Data were collected using a questionnaire with a five-point Likert scale. The independent variables in this study were employee training (X1) and employee development (X2), while the dependent variable was the implementation of quality management (Y). Data analysis was conducted using validity and reliability tests, classical assumption tests, multiple linear regression analysis, t-tests, F-tests, and the coefficient of determination. The data analysis results indicate that employee training has a positive and statistically significant effect on the implementation of quality management, with a calculated t-value of 3.194 and a significance level of 0.002. Employee development also has a positive and statistically significant effect, with a calculated t-value of 4.220 and a significance level of 0.000. Simultaneously, employee training and development have a positive and statistically significant effect on the implementation of quality management, with a calculated F-value of 61.690 and a significance level of 0.000. The coefficient of determination of 0.684 indicates that 68.4% of the variation in the implementation of quality management can be explained by employee training and development, while the remaining 31.6% is explained by other factors outside the research model. These findings highlight the importance of corporate investment in enhancing employee competencies as part of ongoing efforts to improve the implementation of quality management sustainably.

title: From Spectra to Clinical Insight: Raman Spectroscopy in Kidney Transplant Monitoring and Donor Assessment
abstractText: Abstract Purpose of Review Raman spectroscopy and surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) are analytical techniques for non-invasive assessment of kidney transplant health. By producing molecular fingerprints through inelastic light scattering, they’re able to detect biochemical changes associated with graft injury, immune activation, and other relevant pathophysiological changes. This review synthesizes current evidence of Raman-based techniques across three key domains in kidney transplantation: transplant monitoring, donor organ assessment, and evaluation of alloreactive immune activation. Recent Findings Recent studies demonstrate that SERS can be applied to biofluids and can accurately distinguish between transplant states. Additionally, Raman-based analyses of donor-derived samples show potential for predicting transplant outcomes and identifying viable organs despite high-risk features. It has also been shown to differentiate between activated and non-activated T lymphocytes. Summary Raman spectroscopy and SERS represent powerful, non-invasive approaches that have the potential to reduce the reliance on invasive biopsy.

abstractText: The article is devoted to methods for automated recognition of guiding triangles on engineering diagrams of oil and gas fields. Recognition here refers to the detection, localization, and classification of these graphic objects; the output data are the coordinates and the class of the recognized object. A comparative analysis is carried out for classical filters, the one-stage YOLOv11s-seg detector, and the two-stage Mask R-CNN architecture. A synthetic dataset of 10,000 diagrams was used for training and testing, each of which contains triangles with variations in illumination, overlaps, and incomplete contour rendering. The experiments showed that all the models surpass the classical methods in speed and robustness; however, only Mask R-CNN provides a high level of recognition recall (92 %), whereas YOLO reaches 72 %. The most difficult cases proved to be objects with partial overlaps. It is established that Mask R-CNN demonstrates the greatest robustness to these factors and is recommended for use as part of industrial computer-vision systems for automating the digitization of design documentation.

title: Ecology drives the degree of convergence in the gene expression of extremophile fishes
abstractText: Abstract Convergent evolution is common and a testament to the repeatability of evolution. Still, non-convergence is also widespread, and a major question is whether idiosyncratic, lineage-specific changes are reflective of chance events inherent to evolutionary processes, or whether they are influenced by deterministic genetic or ecological factors. To address this question, we quantified the degree of convergence in gene expression across lineages of livebearing fishes (Poeciliidae) that span 40 million years of divergence and have colonized toxic, hydrogen-sulfide-rich springs. We asked whether the degree of convergence across lineage pairs was related to their phylogenetic relatedness and the ecological similarity of their habitats. Using phylogenetic comparative analyses, we showed that the degree of convergence in gene expression was variable across lineage pairs. While closely related lineages did not exhibit higher degrees of convergence than distantly related ones, we uncovered a strong relationship between degree of convergence and the ecological similarity among lineages. These results suggest that variation in environmental conditions that is often overlooked in simplified descriptions of habitat differences can play an important role in shaping adaptive evolution. Our study highlights the importance of multivariate approaches that capture the complexities of selective regimes and organismal responses when assessing the repeatability of evolution.

Biochemically supported diagnosis of Fabry disease in a young adult with unexplained left ventricular hypertrophy: a diagnostic challenge
abstractText: Fabry disease (OMIM #301500) is a rare X-linked lysosomal storage disorder caused by pathogenic variants in the GLA gene, resulting in deficient activity of α-galactosidase A. This enzymatic defect leads to lysosomal glycosphingolipid accumulation and progressive multisystem dysfunction. The clinical manifestations are variable and non-specific, which may delay diagnosis. We report a 29-year-old Malay man who presented with recurrent palpitations, exertional chest pain, dyspnoea and fatigue. The physical examination was unremarkable, and there was no known relevant family history. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated significant concentric left ventricular hypertrophy with markedly reduced native myocardial T1 values. No significant coronary artery abnormalities were identified, raising suspicion of an infiltrative or metabolic cardiomyopathy. Plasma α-galactosidase A activity was markedly reduced at 0.3 nmol/mL/h (reference interval, 2.0–10.0 nmol/mL/h), which, together with the compatible cardiac imaging findings, strongly supported a diagnosis of Fabry disease, although molecular confirmation was unavailable. This case highlights a cardiac-predominant presentation strongly supportive of Fabry disease in a young Malaysian adult without documented classical extracardiac manifestations or a known relevant family history. It underscores the importance of considering Fabry disease in young patients with otherwise unexplained left ventricular hypertrophy and characteristic cardiac magnetic resonance findings. Early recognition is important to facilitate molecular confirmation, family screening and timely consideration of disease-specific management before irreversible organ damage develops.

title: Molecular profiling of ovarian cancer is feasible and provides valuable therapeutic and research information to women in Aotearoa New Zealand
abstractText: aim: Molecular profiling of ovarian cancer is feasible and provides valuable therapeutic and research information to women in Aotearoa New Zealand. method: Sixteen women consecutively diagnosed with apparent advanced ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer underwent molecular profiling as part of INOVATe (Individualised Ovarian Cancer Treatment through Integration of Genomic Pathology into Multidisciplinary Care), an ovarian cancer precision medicine programme conducted in New South Wales, Australia. results: All eligible women who were approached agreed to participate in the study. Molecular profiling was successfully undertaken on tumour tissue samples stored after primary surgery and in two of three core biopsy samples. Six of 9 women (67%) with high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma had tumour samples classified as having homologous recombination deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) repair deficiency, an alteration that predicts response to poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors. Overall, 7/15 (47%) with a sample available for testing had a tier 1 molecular alteration, indicating the potential for a Food and Drug Administration–approved therapy. Additional potentially targetable alterations included CCNE1 gene amplification in two patients with high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma, and PIK3CA mutations in two patients with clear cell ovarian cancer. conclusion: Molecular profiling of ovarian cancer is feasible and provides valuable information that can guide available therapeutic options and selection into clinical trials.

Evolving shear bands in a nonlinear micropolar continuum
abstractText: Abstract Shear bands in inelastic solids are often treated as stationary failure zones whose orientation is fixed at bifurcation, a view reinforced by classical Cauchy continua with softening and no internal length scale, where loss of ellipticity drives deformation into a single planar band. Experiments in granular media, however, increasingly show curved, branching and migrating shear zones. Here, we study finite-strain localization in a geometrically nonlinear micropolar (Cosserat) continuum implemented in an implicit material point method, using a non-associative Drucker–Prager model with a unified yield surface based on a generalized measure of stresses and couple stresses to introduce an intrinsic length scale. Two-dimensional boundary-value problems show that localization need not remain rectilinear or stationary: the active zone can curve, reorient and migrate as the stress state evolves, without ad hoc parameter tuning. Viewed through the microrotation field, the evolving centreline is consistently traced by a near-zero ridge of the band-normal microrotation gradient, which we propose as a natural band-selection rule in the nonlinear micropolar continuum.

title: Residual monomers and volatile leachable substances of conventional and CAD/CAM-fabricated denture base materials — GC-MS analysis and surface characterization
abstractText: Abstract Objectives Methacrylic acid ester-based resins for denture fabrication release residual monomers and leachable substances that may interact with oral tissues. With increasing adoption of CAD/CAM technologies, a systematic comparison of leachable substance profiles and surface characteristics across polymerization methods is needed. Materials and methods This study compared the chemical composition and profiles of leachable substances of four denture materials – autopolymerized, thermal polymerized, milled, and 3D-printed – using gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC–MS). Surface roughness was evaluated by confocal microscopy. Results GC–MS screening detected 24 distinct compounds in the solid specimens. Among the MMA/PMMA-based materials, methyl methacrylate content was highest in the thermally polymerized resin, followed by the autopolymerized and milled materials, and absent from the 3D-printed resin, consistent with its MMA-free formulation. MMA levels in the extracts did not exceed those of the negative control in any group. Surface roughness was comparable on the polished face (R a ≈ 0.21–0.25 μm), consistent with SEM findings but material-dependent on the unpolished, tissue-contacting face (R a 0.37–1.03 μm). Conclusions Both fabrication method and material formulation influence the volatile and semi-volatile extractables of denture resins. As the present GC–MS screening may not reliably capture high-molecular-weight dimethacrylates such as Bis-EMA and UDMA, novel CAD/CAM materials require additional, complementary toxicological evaluation. Clinical relevance The leachable substance profiles of CAD/CAM denture resins, particularly the distinct compounds detected in the 3D-printed material, underscore the need for material-specific biocompatibility data to support informed clinical material selection and patient safety.

title: Coordinated Metabolic Strategies for Green and Efficient Orotic Acid Biomanufacturing in Escherichia coli
abstractText: Abstract Orotic acid (OA) is an intermediate in de novo pyrimidine biosynthesis and a bio-based chemical of interest for nutraceutical, animal nutrition, and biomedical applications. Efficient fermentative OA production, however, remains constrained by carbon loss, insufficient nitrogen assimilation, product-associated stress, and energy-redox imbalance during high-titer production. This study constructed a high-performance Escherichia coli cell factory by coordinating product transport, carbon-nitrogen flux, and energy-redox metabolism. Deletion of the inward OA transporter dctA improved extracellular OA accumulation, while the introduction of a nonoxidative glycolysis (NOG) module, acetyl-phosphate recycling, and byproduct-pathway attenuation reduced overflow carbon loss. Nitrogen assimilation was strengthened by tuning heterologous ammonium transport and balancing NADPH supply. Adenylate metabolism reconstruction and microaerobically responsive expression of vgb and cyoABCDE increased intracellular ATP levels and promoted the NADH/NAD+ redox balance, supporting OA biosynthesis during mid-to-late-stage fed-batch fermentation. OA24 produced 214.2 g/L OA in 42 h in a 5-L bioreactor, with an apparent glucose-based yield of 0.70 g/g glucose and productivity of 5.10 g/L/h; relative to the initial strain Ora21, the yield and productivity increased by 20.7% and 34.2%, respectively. This work provides a carbon-efficient and high-intensity biomanufacturing strategy for OA and related pyrimidine chemicals.

title: First molecular survey of pigs in Victoria, Australia, reveals widespread Cryptosporidium infection, limited Giardia duodenalis occurrence and genotypes with zoonotic potential
abstractText: Abstract Background Cryptosporidium spp. and Giardia duodenalis are enteric protozoan parasites of veterinary and public health significance, yet molecular epidemiological data from Australian pig populations remain limited, and no study has previously been conducted in Victoria. This study estimated prevalences and investigated species composition and genotypic diversity of Cryptosporidium spp. and G. duodenalis in faecal samples collected from pigs across farms in Victoria, Australia. Methods In total, 626 faecal samples were collected from pigs representing multiple age groups across 37 farms in the State of Victoria, Australia. Molecular detection and characterisation were performed using nested PCR targeting the small subunit of the nuclear ribosomal rRNA gene ( SSU ) and gp60 loci for Cryptosporidium and the tpi locus for G. duodenalis , followed by Sanger sequencing. Results Cryptosporidium spp. were detected in 320 samples (51.1%) across 28 farms (76%), with C. scrofarum (77.5%) and C. suis (18.4%) predominating. C. ubiquitum DNA was detected in three faecal samples from pigs on a single farm. Subtyping identified C. suis subtype XXVa-1 and C. ubiquitum subtype XIIa, both previously identified in humans. Giardia duodenalis was detected in seven samples (1.1%) from three farms, with assemblage E ( n = 5) and assemblage A ( n = 2) identified. Cryptosporidium prevalence estimates varied significantly by age group and farming system, being highest in weaners (68.6%) and semi-intensive systems (78.2%) and absent in adult pigs. Conclusions These findings establish the first molecular baseline for Cryptosporidium spp. and G. duodenalis in Victorian pigs, demonstrate the widespread occurrence of Cryptosporidium in pig production systems, identify genotypes with zoonotic potential and highlight the need for ongoing surveillance and targeted parasite management in Australian pig production.

Sir Francis Graham-Smith
abstractText: Abstract Sir Francis Graham-Smith was a towering figure in British astronomy, whose career spanned much of the history of radio astronomy itself. Appointed as the thirteenth Astronomer Royal in 1982 and knighted in 1986, he made foundational contributions to our understanding of radio sources, the interstellar medium, pulsars and the development of radio telescopes. In a multi-faceted career he also made major contributions to science leadership, education, policy and public engagement. As a leader, he established the Isaac Newton Group of telescopes and the Roque de los Muchachos Observatory on La Palma, and his directorship at Jodrell Bank during a critical period ensured the observatory's continued international relevance and scientific excellence. As an educator, he authored numerous textbooks and was a warm mentor to students and junior colleagues. As a policy-former, he served as a pro-vice-chancellor of the University of Manchester and Physical Secretary of the Royal Society. Throughout his long career and retirement, Sir Francis left indelible marks on many people. We will remember his sharp intellect and generosity with time and ideas.

title: Design, uptake, and adaptation of a curated global infant and young child feeding digital health education course to capacitate frontline health workers
abstractText: Abstract Background Health workers have critical roles in delivering quality infant and young child feeding (IYCF) services, which include skilled counseling for breastfeeding and complementary feeding. However, health workers’ access to quality IYCF training has been limited. Although IYCF training opportunities are available, most are delivered in conventional learning set-ups, and accessing these trainings can be challenging for many health workers due to restrictions in schedules, inaccessibility of training locations, and inadequate training language proficiency. During the COVID-19 pandemic, the advantages of utilizing e-learning platforms for health worker training have been highlighted, including time, location, and schedule flexibility, increased access for learners, the opportunity for standardized course delivery, and completion monitoring. Methods Recognizing a gap in accessible online guidance and support for IYCF capacity strengthening for health workers, Alive & Thrive and its partners curated available training materials from authoritative health organizations into a practical, competency-based, and self-paced e-learning course. Using the Analysis, Design, Development, Implementation, and Evaluation (ADDIE) model for course development, and with support from a digital solutions service provider and a technical steering committee composed of international experts, available training materials were translated into an e-learning format to create a self-paced course for IYCF. The final product is packaged as the “IYCF E-learning Course: Investing in Child Nutrition” and is available in Arabic, English, and French. A country adaptation of the IYCF e-learning course was also made in Jordan in 2023, through which the course was translated into Arabic. Results From its launch in June 2019 to January 2021, about 2,000 enrollees from 106 countries accessed the Arabic, English, and French versions of the course package. Positive feedback from users was received on the inclusive nature of the course content and imagery, as well as the breadth of resources available. Meanwhile, the adapted version for Jordan recorded 1,123 enrollees from 33 countries as of June 2024. The course is currently hosted on the UNICEF Agora platform. Conclusions The development and experience monitoring the uptake of the IYCF E-learning Course has demonstrated the utility of an extensive e-learning course package that can be further adapted to fit specific country-level or local contexts.
